articles.title: Will Dodgers Recover From Unsuccessful 3-Peat? MLB History Says It's Complicated
articles.summary: Will the Los Angeles Dodgers get back on track after failing to three-peat? Here's what happened the last 10 times an MLB team was in the situation.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers came up eight wins short of three-peating. With the Dodgers – who were the defending, back-to-back World Series champions – being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series, the 1998-2000 New York Yankees remain the last MLB team to three-peat. Will the Dodgers bounce back in 2027? Here's what happened to the last 10 MLB teams that repeated as World Series champions but didn't win a third consecutive championship. 1992-93 Toronto Blue Jays The Toronto Blue Jays were the rippers of the American League East in the early 1990s. John Olerud, Roberto Alomar and Joe Carter, accompanied by Dave Winfield in 1992 and Paul Molitor in 1993, made for one of MLB's most fearsome offenses, with Juan Guzmán and Pat Hentgen, among others, taking the hill in their starting rotation. Toronto beat the Atlanta Braves in six games in the 1992 World Series and the Philadelphia Phillies in six games in the 1993 World Series, which came after the Blue Jays were eliminated in the AL Championship Series twice from 1989-91. What happened after winning back-to-back titles? The Blue Jays went 55-60 before a players' strike ended the 1994 season. They then had four consecutive losing seasons, the bulk of the aforementioned sluggers were gone in the ensuing years and the franchise wouldn't make the playoffs again until 2015. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1977-78 New York Yankees After being swept by the Cincinnati Reds in the 1976 World Series, the Yankees got back to doing one of the things they did best: beating the Dodgers in the World Series. In both 1977 and 1978, the Yankees won 100 games in the regular season and beat the Dodgers in the World Series in six games. The consecutive championship triumphs improved the Yankees to 8-2 all time against the Dodgers in the World Series. This rendition of the former New York baseball rivals – the Dodgers moved from Brooklyn to Los Angeles in 1958 – was defined by "Mr. October," Yankees outfielder Reggie Jackson. While Yankees shortstop Bucky Dent won 1978 World Series MVP honors, Jackson blasted two home runs and drove in eight runs in the series, which came after he obliterated five home runs and won MVP honors in the 1977 World Series. With that said, the Yankees missed the playoffs in 1979 and were swept by the Kansas City Royals in the 1980 AL Championship Series before losing to the Dodgers in six games in the 1981 World Series. New York wouldn't make the playoffs again until 1995. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1975-76 Cincinnati Reds After years of postseason heartbreak, the Big Red Machine won back-to-back titles in 1975 and '76. As previously alluded to, Pete Rose, Johnny Bench, George Foster, Joe Morgan & Co. swept the Yankees in the 1976 World Series, which saw Bench blast two home runs and go 8 for 15 in the series en route to earning World Series MVP honors. The year before, the Reds squeaked past the Boston Red Sox in seven games in the 1975 World Series, with Rose hitting .370 in the series and winning MVP honors. Then, though, the Reds missed the playoffs in each of the next two seasons, were swept by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the 1979 NLCS and wouldn't make the playoffs again until their 1990 championship series. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1961-62 New York Yankees Bill Mazeroski walked off the Yankees in Game 7 of the 1960 World Series, which resulted in New York winning back-to-back World Series in rage. In 1961, the Yankees won 109 games and beat the Reds in five games in the World Series, with them then beating the San Francisco Giants in seven games in the 1962 Fall Classic. However, the Dodgers swept the Yankees in the 1963 World Series, with Sandy Koufax, Don Drysdale and Johnny Podres holding New York to just four runs. The ensuing year, the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Yankees in seven games in the 1964 World Series. New York wouldn't make the playoffs again until 1976. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1929-30 Philadelphia Athletics The Athletics were a force to be reckoned with. Al Simmons, Jimmie Foxx, Mickey Cochrane and Bing Miller spearheaded a potent A's offense, while the franchise had southpaw Lefty Grove emerging into a Hall of Fame force on the rubber. They beat the Chicago Cubs in five games in the 1929 World Series and the Cardinals in six games in the 1930 Fall Classic. Ironically, the A's won a still-franchise-record 107 games in 1931, but it ended with them losing to the Cardinals in seven games in the World Series, highlighted by outfielder/third baseman Pepper Martin hitting .500 in the series. The Athletics wouldn't make the playoffs again until 1971. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1927-28 New York Yankees Yeah, the Yankees have won a few titles here and there. After losing to the Cardinals in seven games in the 1926 World Series, the Yankees swept consecutive World Series in 1927 and 1928 over the Pirates and Cardinals. While they missed the playoffs from 1929-31, New York got off the mat in 1932, winning 107 games and ultimately sweeping the Cubs in the World Series, adding yet another ring to Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig's would-be deep collection. That was also the series when Ruth "called his shot" on a home run. The Yankees would commence another three-year playoff drought from 1933-35, but they followed it up by winning four consecutive World Series. Suffice to say: New York got back on track. Verdict: Bounced back 1921-22 New York Giants The New York Giants opened the decade of the 1920s with a bang. Led by the offensive firepower of George Kelly, Dave Bancroft, Irish Meusel, Ross Youngs and Frankie Frisch, the Giants defeated the Yankees in both the 1921 (eight games) and 1922 World Series (five games). The Giants returned to the World Series in each of the next two seasons but lost both times, with the Yankees beating them in six games in 1923 and the Washington Nationals winning in seven games against them in 1924. They wouldn't make the playoffs for eight consecutive seasons before beating the Nationals in five games in the 1933 World Series. Verdict: Didn't bounce back 1915-16 Boston Red Sox Arguably the best era of Boston Red Sox baseball came in the decade of the 1910s. Three years after winning the 1912 World Series, the Red Sox were victorious again, beating the Philadelphia Phillies in five games in the 1915 World Series and the Brooklyn Robins in five games in the 1916 Fall Classic. In both seasons, Boston rode elite starting pitching, which included Ruth (originally a primary starting pitcher), Smoky Joe Wood (in 1915), Ernie Shore and Rube Foster, among other hurlers. After missing the playoffs in 1917, the Red Sox beat the Cubs in six games in the 1918 World Series. Granted, a 28-year playoff drought and an 86-year championship drought would begin in 1919. Still, Boston won the next season after failing to execute the three-peat. Verdict: Bounced back 1910-11 Philadelphia Athletics The Athletics came of age in 1910. In said year, they won a then-franchise record 102 games and defeated the Cubs in five games in the 1910 World Series for their first franchise triumph. They then won 101 games in 1911 and beat the Giants in six games in the Fall Classic. Home Run Baker (what a name!), Eddie Collins, Danny Murphy and Bris Lord led the charge for their lineup, while Jack Coombs, Eddie Plank, Charles Bender and Cy Morgan, among others, formed a stellar starting rotation. Now, the A's missed the playoffs in 1912, but they'd get back to and win the World Series in 1913, knocking off the Giants in five games. The Athletics would reach the World Series again in 1914. Verdict: Bounced back 1907-08 Chicago Cubs Starting pitching was the name of the game for the Cubs in the late 1900s. Chicago beat the Detroit Tigers in five games in both the 1907 and 1908 World Series, with historical pitching on its side: Hall of Famer Mordecai Brown, Ed Reulbach, Jack Pfiester, Orvall Overall and Carl Lundgren, to name some. All that said, while they reached the World Series in 1910 after missing the playoffs in 1909, the Cubs would lose to the Athletics in five games. For any history buffs, the Cubs wouldn't win the World Series again until 2016. articles.title: How Has Ohio State Star WR Jeremiah Smith Performed Against Indiana?
articles.summary: Here's how Ohio State Buckeyes superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has performed against the Indiana Hoosiers in his career.
articles.body: "Where's Jeremiah Smith?" That's the question every defense has to answer when they play the No. 4-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes. In Week 7 of the 2026 college football season, that team will be the defending-national champion and currently No. 5-ranked Indiana Hoosiers, who have won 22 consecutive games dating back to last season. Kickoff for the Big Ten showdown, which will be the first time the two teams square off against each other since last season's Big Ten Championship game, is Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on FOX, with FOX's "Big Noon Kickoff" on site in Bloomington. Here's how Smith has performed against Indiana defensive coordinator Bryant Haines' unit: Jeremiah Smith vs. Indiana (2025) In short: Smith ripped apart the Hoosiers' defense when the two teams met in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. Smith reeled in eight receptions for 144 yards – 18.0 yards per reception – marking his then-fifth 100-plus-yard receiving game of the season. The problem? Ohio State lost to Indiana, 13-10, shortly after a 7:57 drive ended with a 22-yard missed field goal from Buckeyes kicker Jayden Fielding with 2:48 remaining in the fourth quarter. Both the Buckeyes and Hoosiers were 12-0 entering the conference title game. The win was Indiana's first against Ohio State since 1988. Jeremiah Smith vs. Indiana (2024) A Week 13 matchup in 2024 between Ohio State and Indiana saw the Hoosiers enter the game at 10-0, but the Buckeyes put a stop to that undefeated streak. As part of a 38-15 win, the Buckeyes outgained the Hoosiers in total yards, 316-151, with Ohio State quarterback Will Howard completing 22 of 26 passes. That said, Smith only had three receptions for 34 yards, with him also recording a 12-yard carry. The 34 receiving yards are the second-lowest mark of Smith's three-year collegiate career. Jeremiah Smith's Ohio State Records Through Ohio State's six games this season, Smith has totaled 48 receptions for 916 yards (19.1 yards per reception) and 11 touchdowns, which all lead the Big Ten and are second in the nation altogether. Over the Buckeyes' Week 4 and 5 victories over the Illinois Fighting Illini and Iowa Hawkeyes, Smith averaged a whopping 11.5 receptions for 211.5 yards and three touchdowns per contest. According to FOX Sports Research, Smith is just the second player in Big Ten history to have back-to-back, 200-plus-yard receiving games, the other player being Indiana's Ty Fryfrogle (2020). Furthermore, Smith is now the Buckeyes' all-time leader in receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He's two receiving touchdowns away from being first in Big Ten history; Michigan Wolverines wide receiver Braylon Edwards is first with 39 receiving scores. Earlier this week, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti expressed that there's "no one" like Smith "playing at this level." Smith previously led the Big Ten in receiving yards in 2024 (1,315) and 2025 (1,243), receptions in 2025 (87) and receiving touchdowns in 2024 (15). articles.title: Ohio State's Ryan Day Welcomes College Football Playoff Expansion
articles.summary: Ryan Day is embracing the challenges and opportunities of the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams.
articles.body: When Ohio State reached the 2024 College Football Playoff national championship game, it became the first team to navigate the 12-team CFP field to win a trophy. Now, Buckeyes coach Ryan Day is welcoming the idea of competing in a field twice that size. With the anticipation that the CFP will expand to include 24 teams, Day showed support of the idea. "It's great for college football for a lot of reasons," he said, appearing on FOX Sports' "The Herd With Colin Cowherd" on Friday. "More teams are involved and relevant. I think it's great for fanbases, overall." The 24-team field would provide leeway to teams that stumble early in the season, potentially opening the door for three-loss teams to compete in the postseason. The counterpoint might be that it would diminish the competition of first-round matchups, but it would also incentivize scheduling better nonconference opponents. For example, Ohio State and Texas played in consecutive seasons, splitting the series. In 2025, the Longhorns' loss to the Buckeyes — before going on to lose twice in SEC play — was the difference between them qualifying for the 12-team CFP. If they had faced a less-competitive nonconference opponent early on, the Longhorns may have played deep into January. The Buckeyes, who lost to Texas this season in Week 2, could experience that same fate. If Ohio State loses to Indiana this Saturday and suffers another loss in the regular season or the Big Ten championship game, a three-loss record could leave them out of the CFP field. "The expansion allows all of us to play some of those nonconference games earlier in the year, which is good for the game," Day said. "Facing a great team early offers clarity to a coaching staff," Cowherd emphasized in agreement. "That's what you really want as a staff. It's hard to get those winning by four touchdowns." A more competitive schedule could help teams be more polished as the year progresses and the games matter more. In addition, they'd have experience playing the caliber of opponent they'd be set to face in the CFP. "The way things go now, your team is growing. We're a different team than we were earlier in the season. Indiana's a different team than they were earlier in the season. So as you continue to evolve — you know you want to be playing your best football at the end of the season," Day said. The CFP's expansion to 24 teams now seems a matter of when not if. Day and the Buckeyes are getting ahead of that, embracing the challenges and opportunities it will bring. articles.title: Rays-Guardians Postponed: When Will ALCS Game 4 Be Played?
articles.summary: Game 4 of the American League Championship Series has been postponed because of rain.
articles.body: Game 4 of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians was postponed because of rain Friday night. Major League Baseball was hoping there would be a three-hour window of dry weather to get the game in, but the showers never let up. "It never cleared out the way they were hoping. It started to get later in the hour, and MLB and I think both clubs did everything they could to try to get it in," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "Made the most sense, like, at this point and this hour, with no guarantee that there wasn’t another band coming." When Will ALCS Game 4 Be Played? The teams will resume their playoff series Saturday at 8 p.m. ET. According to FOX Weather, Saturday's forecast with morning clouds followed by afternoon sun. Highs will be in the low 50s and lows in the upper 30s. Game 5 will also be at Progressive Field on Sunday at 5 p.m., and Game 6, if necessary, on Monday at 8 p.m. in St. Petersburg, Florida. A potential Game 7 would also be played Tuesday, 8 p.m. in St. Petersburg, Florida. "We knew how many days ago that today was going to be a challenge. Numerous weather calls, numerous back and forths, and ultimately MLB decided we needed to wait it out," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "Obviously it’s an important game, and we need to make sure we’re doing everything we can to play the games when they’re scheduled. But MLB ultimately decided to wait this one out." It is the first time an ALCS game has been postponed since 2019, when the New York Yankees were hosting the Houston Astros. The Guardians have a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series after Petey Halpin’s two-run homer propelled them to a 3-2 victory in Game 3 on Thursday afternoon. Who Will Pitch In Saturday's Game? Both teams will stick with their scheduled Game 4 starters from Friday. Cleveland will go with a bullpen game, with Shawn Armstrong being the opener. Nick Martinez will pitch for Tampa Bay. It will be Armstrong’s fifth appearance this postseason. The right-hander has allowed only one hit in 5 1/3 innings with five strikeouts. Armstrong thought his season was done in late July when he strained a calf muscle, but he returned during the final week of the regular season. Armstrong was drafted by Cleveland in the 18th round in 2011 and made his big league debut four years later. He was traded to Seattle in 2017 and spent time with four other organizations, including Tampa Bay, before signing with the Guardians this season. "I think I said it to (Erik) Sabrowski, whenever we were standing in the outfield in Game 2 in Tampa — obviously I played here, I got drafted here, coming back here and being able to be in this situation is — words can’t describe it," Armstrong said before Game 3 on Thursday. Martinez started Game 3 of the Division Series against the New York Yankees. He went 3 2/3 innings, allowing two runs on five hits with a walk and three strikeouts. The right-hander was 15-6 during the regular season and ranked sixth in the AL with a 3.10 ERA. He was third in the AL with 26 starts in which he allowed three runs or fewer. "It’s just like my starts throughout the year; it’s going to be a dogfight going in, just to see how many outs I can get for this team. It’s important," he said Thursday. NL Champs Brewers Await In World Series The teams might have to play the final four games of the series without a day off, culminating in a potential Game 7 on Tuesday. That could be welcome news for the Milwaukee Brewers, who have a week off before they open the World Series at home on Oct. 23 against the Cleveland-Tampa Bay winner. Milwaukee is in the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982 after completing a four-game sweep of the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series on Thursday night. "We’ve got four games in a row. We have an opportunity to win some games and move on. And that’s all we’re focused on," Vogt said. Reporting by The Associated Press. articles.title: España se queda sin final del Mundial tras caer en los penaltis ante Argentina
articles.standfirst: El partido acaba 2-2 y se decide por 2-1 a favor de la selección albiceleste en los lanzamientos
articles.summary: El partido acaba 2-2 y se decide por 2-1 a favor de la selección albiceleste en los lanzamientos
articles.body: La tanda de penaltis dejó a España sin el pase a la final del Mundial de hockey patines que se disputa dentro de los World Skate Games de Asunción (Paraguay). La selección masculina cayó ante Argentina (2-2 y 2-1 en los penaltis), en una reedición de la final de al anterior edición mundialista, y no podrá reeditar el título. Argentina se adelantó en el marcador antes del primer minuto gracias a un tanto de Ezequiel Mena. Iván Morales, a un pase de Pol Manrubia, puso el empate en el minuto 15. La igualdad fue la nota dominante del choque hasta que Biel Llanes puso por delante a España a falta de 10 minutos. La selección albiceleste logró el empate a 111 segundos del final. Lucas Ordóñez lanzó un penalti, Ballart lo detuvo, pero el rechace lo aprovechó el propio Ordóñez para marcar y llevar el partido a la prórroga. El tiempo extra no alteró el marcador y los penaltis decidieron. Argentina empezó la tanda. Ordónez marcó. Le tocó a España. El tiro de Carballeira no entró. Martínez lanzó y detuvo Ballart. Grau anotó y puso el 1-1 tras dos penaltis para cada selección. Ballart volvió a hacerse grande para evitar el gol de Romero. Acevedo hizo lo propio al tiro de Bargalló. Rampull anotó y puso el 2-1. Llanes mandó fuera su penalti. Argentina tenía la opción de acabar la tanda si marcaba.Facundo Bridge se topó de nuevo con Ballart. Manrubia tenía en su mano igualar pero Acevedo se lo impidió y Argentina pasó a la final. La otra semifinal cayó del lado de Francia que se impuso a Portugal por 6-4. Será la primera vez desde 1997 que ni España ni Portugal estarán en la final del Mundial. Ambos se medirán por el bronce este domingo a partir de las 21:15 horas. articles.title: Rio Ferdinand brutally trolled by fans as ‘disgrace’ after “pick up ya t**s” fat-shaming row with Manchester United content creator
articles.summary: Rio Ferdinand has faced a major backlash after becoming involved in a social media clash with Manchester United content creator Saeed TV.
articles.body: Rio Ferdinand has faced a major backlash after becoming involved in a social media clash with Manchester United content creator Saeed TV. The former Manchester United defender was accused of fat-shaming the influencer after responding to criticism of his silence on the club’s ownership.Ferdinand hit back after Saeed TV told him to “Stop yapping and call out the owners!” The former England international replied with a personal comment about Saeed’s weight. His response has since triggered strong reactions from fans, with some calling the remark unacceptable while others defended Ferdinand.Rio Ferdinand’s response sparks huge reaction from Manchester United fansThe controversy began after Rio Ferdinand shared a picture of himself with Manchester United manager Michael Carrick. He also quoted Carrick, who had recently said, “It is not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player and anyone else who works at the club.”It is unclear exactly why Ferdinand shared the message. However, it came after recent criticism surrounding Manchester United’s leadership and squad.Lisandro Martinez has also spoken out about the club this week. The defender reportedly questioned the strength of the squad and made strong comments about the club’s leadership.Saeed TV was unhappy with Ferdinand’s post. He questioned why the former defender had not been more vocal about Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.He commented, “Stop yapping and call out the owners!”Ferdinand responded sharply. He wrote, “Stop yapping and pick up ya t**s, ya out a breath typing!”The response quickly attracted attention online. Many fans accused Ferdinand of crossing a line by making a comment about Saeed’s body.One fan wrote on X, “Rio Ferdinand is an absolute disgrace. Imagine being SO blind that you have to resort to this type of nonsense.”Another wrote, “That's a very very low personal blow from Rio. Uncalled for.” A third commented, “That’s poor from Rio.”Saeed later posted a response video. He criticised Ferdinand for the way he handled the disagreement and questioned his behaviour as a public figure.He said, “You are a grown man and this is the response you put on social media. You have got kids watching you. You are a role model to so many around the world, and yet this is how you conduct yourself around the world. It’s absolutely embarrassing.”He added, “You’ve got people around you who respect you. What is there to respect when you’re speaking like this on social media? It doesn’t affect me because I’ve been through a lot on social media and above all, I’ve been racially abused, so I’ve got thick skin. For me to hold you accountable and for you to resort to that… it tells everything about you.”Saeed also suggested that Ferdinand avoids strongly criticising United’s leadership because he wants to maintain his access to the club.However, not everyone sided with Saeed. articles.title: Security officer sues WWE and Montez Ford over unwanted on-air lap dance, claims shared footage led to humiliation and kids’ bullying
articles.summary: A Cook County sheriff's officer is suing WWE and wrestler Montez Ford after an unwanted lap dance during Monday Night Raw led to public humiliation and bullying of his children. The lawsuit alleges emotional distress and violation of the Illinois Right of Publicity Act.
articles.body: A Cook County sheriff’s officer has sued WWE and wrestler Montez Ford over an alleged unwanted sexualised dance during Monday Night Raw, claiming the televised incident led to public humiliation and left his children being mocked at school. The lawsuit centres on footage from a July event in Illinois, which the plaintiff says spread online after WWE and Ford shared it.A ringside encounter that became the subject of a lawsuitNoel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer who also works private security, was assigned to the July 6, 2026, episode of Monday Night Raw at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, near Chicago. According to the lawsuit, a WWE employee instructed him to take a position closer to ringside before the Street Profits’ entrance.The tag-team duo, Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins, were making their way to the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, allegedly approached Lucas and performed an unwanted lap dance during the Netflix broadcast. The complaint says Ford danced immediately in front of and over Lucas, repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis.The lawsuit describes the encounter as “a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.’”It further alleges Ford moved progressively closer to Lucas as the dance continued, with his “left inner thigh repeatedly rub[bing] against Plaintiff’s leg.” The footage appeared to show Lucas looking uncomfortable before later cracking a faint smile, although the lawsuit alleges that the performance was unscripted and took place without his consent.The footage spread online, and Lucas says the consequences followed him homeThe interaction was not included in the current Netflix replay of the July 6 programme, which cuts to a commercial break early in the Street Profits’ entrance. However, a clip circulated online, including through WWE’s and Ford’s social media accounts. Lucas alleges that the video attracted hundreds of thousands of views and made him recognisable to members of the public.According to the complaint, Lucas encountered people at his full-time courthouse job who recognised him from the clip and mocked him by thrusting their hips towards him, imitating the movements Ford had allegedly performed. The lawsuit also says Lucas’s children were “mocked and ridiculed” at school because of the video.Lucas alleges that he has suffered “humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress” and continues to experience distress because the footage remains publicly available. His complaint also argues that WWE and Ford used his visible image for commercial purposes without authorisation, allegedly violating the Illinois Right of Publicity Act.The complaint names WWE, Ford and a company subsidiaryLucas filed the lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Cook County, naming WWE, Crawford and its subsidiary Event Services, LLC, as defendants. The complaint lists 14 counts, including allegations of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.The lawsuit seeks unspecified monetary and punitive damages, reimbursement of legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using Lucas’s identity. These are allegations in a civil complaint, rather than findings established by a court.WWE had not immediately responded to a request for comment, according to the report. The case is scheduled for a management hearing on December 10.Lucas’s lawyer says he was working to support his familyLucas’s second job brought him to the arena. Alongside his work for the Cook County Sheriff’s Department, he supervises a team of security guards for Monterrey Security, the private firm that assigned him to the event.In a press release provided to POST Wrestling, Lucas’s attorney Whitney Barr said: “Like so many law enforcement officers, Mr. Lucas works a second job in order to better provide for his children.”Lucas is represented by Barr and Alexis Martin of Caffarelli & Martin Ltd. After falling to the UCLA Bruins , 17-15, in Week 6 for their second loss of the year, the Oregon Ducks find themselves unranked heading into their Week 7 home date with the Nebraska Cornhuskers . And the Cornhuskers will be no easy opponent, as they enter with a 5-1 record after giving the Indiana Hoosiers a run for their money last week.

The Ducks had a lot to clean up this week, especially offensively after they turned the ball over six times prior to the final play of the game. The quarterback situation is the biggest question, as head coach Dan Lanning has yet to name a starter with Dylan Raiola , Brock Thomas and Akili Smith Jr. all reportedly competing for the nod. Raiola stunk it up last week while Thomas was excellent in relief. Smith is the wildcard, uber talented but has yet to appear in a competitive game in his career (he threw four passes against FCS Portland State).

The defense, though they allowed a few chunk plays, was stout against the Bruins and will look to repeat that effort against a talented Cornhuskers offensive unit.

articles.title: Pirates Top Prospects No. 15: Lonnie White Jr. Bounces Back in Big Way
articles.summary: This is one in a series of stories breaking down PBN’s Top 30 Pirates prospects. Lonnie White Jr. was committed […]
articles.body:
This is one in a series of stories breaking down PBN's Top 30 Pirates prospects .

Lonnie White Jr. was committed to play baseball and football at Penn State when the Pirates selected him in the second round of the 2021 draft. They thought so highly of him that they signed him to an overslot deal of $1.5 million to pry him away from the Nittany Lions.

He got his first taste of professional baseball in 2021 but missed essentially all of 2022 with an injury. Injuries continued to be a problem for White, but he still performed well in the Florida Complex League and Low-A Bradenton in 2023.

But White hit just .167 with a .614 OPS with High-A Greensboro in the hitter-friendly South Atlantic League in 2024. He improved back with Greensboro in 2025, but only marginally. White batted .220/.320/.394 with 12 home runs, 39 RBI and 23 steals. Injuries again played a part, limiting him to a combined 171 games between the two seasons.

Aided by good health, White broke out this year. The 23-year-old began the year with Greensboro but quickly earned a promotion to Double-A Altoona. In 91 games post-promotion, White slashed .262/.366/.500 with 16 doubles, two triples, 19 home runs, 48 RBI and 12 steals.

White, who ranked fourth among Pirates' minor-leaguers with 26 combined home runs between Greensboro and Altoona, finished fourth in the Eastern League in slugging percentage, tied for fourth OPS (.866) and ninth in OBP.

White is extremely athletic. Most people capable of playing Division I football are. But health has always been the biggest factor holding White back from reaching his full potential.

With a mostly healthy season, White showed the type of player he can be. He's back on the prospect radar as a player the Pirates are hoping can one day help contribute. He possesses an intriguing mix of some power, speed and defense.

articles.title: Michigan State Is An 8.5-Point Home Underdog. Three Keys To Win
articles.summary: Michigan State hosts No. 25 Northwestern down its top four cornerbacks, and three keys could still swing it. #GoGreen
articles.body:
Pat Fitzgerald and the 2-4 Spartans are still looking for their first Big Ten win of the season after losing to Illinois 38-37 in overtime last week. Michigan State vs. Northwestern now asks a defense down its top four cornerbacks and top three linebackers to slow the newly ranked No. 25 Wildcats, led by former Spartans quarterback Aidan Chiles, who has Northwestern at 4-1.

Force Chiles' First Interception Of The Season

Aidan Chiles has been nearly perfect for Northwestern this season: nine touchdowns and no interceptions. Chiles also leads the Big Ten in completion percentage at 71.4% . While Chiles hasn't thrown a pick this season, he has experience throwing them in East Lansing. In 2024, he threw six of his 11 interceptions at home , and he added one more in Spartan Stadium last season before he was benched.

While the Spartans have only two interceptions this season , the one last week helped swing momentum and set up overtime for MSU. Michigan State safety Devin Vaught grabbed an interception with 1:41 left in the third quarter and returned it 37 yards to the Illinois 11-yard line. The offense responded right away, with Jaziun Patterson rushing for a touchdown on the first play after the interception.

Michigan State quarterback Alessio Milivojevic has struggled to find his groove, but he worked efficiently last week. He completed 84.6% of his passes , his first game over 80% this season, and he enters Saturday with 1,047 passing yards. He also threw two touchdowns after a three-week drought with none. If the Spartans want a chance to win, Milivojevic will need to bring his improved play from last week and not regress to his previous level.

The Spartans' injury report is already lengthy , with multiple position groups forced to start multiple backups. The cornerback room has the most absences, with four players ruled out. The linebacker room is next, with three out, including Jordan Hall. The Detroit News reported in September that Hall wears the green dot that carries coach-to-player communication on defense, and that Brady Pretzlaff filled that role when Hall was unavailable. Both are out Saturday, so it is unknown who Pat Fitzgerald and Michigan State defensive coordinator Joe Rossi will put in the headset.

Michigan State will need to remain as healthy as possible and not add names to the lengthy injury report. Especially on defense, the Spartans are already playing third-stringers and lack the depth to lose any additional positions. While injuries are hard to control, Fitzgerald will need to find the best way to keep his players safe.

How To Watch Michigan State vs. Northwestern

Matchup: No. 25 Northwestern Wildcats 4-1 (1-1) at Michigan State Spartans 2-4 (0-3)

Radio: WJR 760 AM (Spartan Media Network)

Odds: Northwestern -8.5, total 49.5 as of Friday afternoon

If Michigan State wins, it is because they can force Aidan Chiles into his old turnover ways. Chiles has worked efficiently under Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly; Pat Fitzgerald will need to get who's left of his defense ready. Milivojevic will also need to play well to match the high-scoring Wildcat offense.

While the Spartan offense may work well against Northwestern, their defense seems to be missing too many starters to slow down a Wildcat team that has scored at least 30 points in all but one game this season. Northwestern will likely win, though a high-scoring battle is possible.

Our Pick: Northwestern 38 – Michigan State 27

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton drops ruthless three-word insult on Milwaukee Bucks star in OT defeat
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star player Tyrese Haliburton is known for always smiling and dropping big performances on the court, but against the Milwaukee Bucks, it’s al...
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star player Tyrese Haliburton is known for always smiling and dropping big performances on the court, but against the Milwaukee Bucks, it's always business for him.

The Pacers took on the Bucks in their fifth preseason game. Haliburton had already returned to the lineup against the OKC Thunder but the team decided to give him another chance to get some games under his belt, which is why he started against the Bucks.

He dropped another good performance, scoring 17 points and making 6 assists, while shooting 50% from the field. While his performance was top-tier, Haliburton had an incident with a Bucks player that got heated in the first quarter.

Haliburton's relationship with the Milwaukee Bucks franchise has not been so great and it is due to how he has managed to beat them twice in the postseason. His father infamously celebrated winning the first-round series against the Bucks in the 2024-25 season by running onto the floor with a custom tower which had his son's face and yelling at Giannis Antetokounmpo's face.

The Greek Freak is no more in Milwaukee but Haliburton seems to be continuing the rivalry with the Bucks. In the first quarter, he was slightly pushed to the floor by Bucks guard Ryan Rollins.

Haliburton took exception to this and got up to use swear words on Rollins , while his teammates tried to intervene and calm the situation down.

The game ended with the Bucks taking away the victory in overtime, but Haliburton would certainly return in the regular season for his revenge on Rollins.

In his absence, the Pacers finished with a 19-63 record and ended 13th in the Eastern Conference. However, with him in the line-up, many have high expectations for the Pacers and Haliburton will be focused on helping his team meet them.

articles.summary: The latest injury updates on Caleb Williams, Tyler Warren and more.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren lead the list of players at their respective positions who are uncertain to play in NFL Week 6.

Williams has been recovering from a hamstring injury for weeks now, and Warren was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, which leaves his status uncertain.

Along with those two, we'll check out injury updates on Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq.

Here's what we know about all four players in advance of Sunday.

Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) looks on during warmups before the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field. Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Caleb Williams turned in his first full practice since his hamstring injury in Week 2 on Wednesday, and he followed that up with two more full sessions to close out the week.

However, Williams isn't in the clear yet, as he is listed as questionable to play on Sunday.

Head coach Ben Johnson has sounded optimistic about Williams' chances of playing all week, and Williams reposted a TikTok hype video on Friday that seems to suggest he's back.

We'll see if there's any clarity on Saturday, but if not we'll know for sure no later than Sunday at 11:30 a.m. ET, when the Bears put out their inactives.

Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren (84) practices before the at Lucas Oil Stadium. Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Tyler Warren was a late addition to the injury report this week with a groin issue.

The injury occurred at practice on Friday, according to ESPN's Stephen Holder , and the Colts tight end is now questionable to play .

Being added to the injury report late in the week is typically a bad sign for a player's chances of suiting up. We'd put his odds of playing at 50/50.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) drops back to pass during the first half against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium. Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

There was a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter early in the week that Lamar Jackson, who is still dealing with an ankle injury, had a real chance to suit up .

However, the optimism for the Ravens quarterback was short-lived and he did not log a single practice before he was ruled out for Week 6 .

It'll be another week of backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley as Jackson turns his attention to a possible Week 7 return.

New York Jets tight end and 1st round draft pick Kenyon Sadiq (16) takes a water break during a practice for the New York Jets at their training facility on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in Florham Park. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Kenyon Sadiq came down with a concussion during the Week 5 win over the Cleveland Browns.

The Jets tight end started off limited over the first two days but showed progress on Friday with a full practice before drawing a questionable tag .

We'll see if Sadiq can get cleared on Saturday, but for now he's trending in the right direction to play on Sunday.

articles.title: 3 keys to victory: Michigan Football vs Penn State
articles.summary: Michigan Football returns this afternoon to host Penn State. Here are the 3 keys to victory for the Wolverines:
articles.body:
Both Michigan and Penn State are heading into Saturday's matchup without a win in conference play. The Wolverines are looking to right the ship, especially on offense, coming out of the bye week. Aside from 2020, the Nittany Lions haven't had a losing season since 2004 and could fall under .500 with a loss at The Big House.

Both teams are going into their matchup with a ton of pressure to deliver for two fan bases that are certainly getting antsy. As Michigan looks for its first Big Ten win of the season in a matchup between two first-year coaches, here are the keys to victory against Penn State.

Now, I've been saying this for basically the entire season. But against Penn State, the run game is really going to matter.

Michigan's offensive line is still a bit banged up with Andrew Sprague still out and multiple players questionable for the game — Andrew Babalola, Jake Guarnera and Brady Norton, with Nathan Efobi listed as probable. But that shouldn't be an excuse for running backs Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter, who are both still looking for a true breakout performance.

Marshall still hasn't had a game with more than 60 rushing yards, and Hiter has only averaged more than four yards per carry in one game so far. Penn State has the 105th-best run defense in the country, so the Wolverines are going to need to exploit that weakness because the pass defense ranks sixth in the country and will make it nearly impossible for Bryce Underwood to get going.

The Wolverines don't need both Marshall and Hiter to break out and have 100 yards. But against a pass defense as strong as the Nittany Lions, Michigan is going to need to generate offense somehow — and that should start with the run game.

The turnover battle has been a struggle all season long for Michigan. The only game in which the Wolverines won the turnover battle was against Oklahoma, and it was one of the main reasons they won. The interception by cornerback Jyaire Hill allowed the Wolverines to score the game-winning touchdown a few plays later.

Then in the last game, Underwood threw two crucial interceptions at the beginning of the second half against Minnesota that accounted for a 10-point swing and, ultimately, the game. Michigan's offense also only scored seven points, as the other touchdown came from a pick-six by linebacker Nathaniel Staehling. Turnovers had a huge impact on the Wolverines' loss to the Golden Gophers and was the Achilles' Heel in an offense that never truly found its footing.

So far this season, Michigan has committed nine turnovers, ranking 102nd nationally with an average of 1.8 per game. Penn State had one turnover in the first four games before having three in the last two. The Wolverines' defense has done a better job of forcing turnovers in recent weeks and will need to keep that up while the offense limits mistakes.

Michigan has the fifth-best pass defense in the nation (146.8 passing yards per game) as well as the eighth-best yards per pass attempt (5.7 yards). Against Minnesota's Drake Lindsey, the Wolverines only allowed 136 passing yards to a quarterback that has thrown for more than 200 in all five other games he's played. Iowa quarterback Hank Brown is the only quarterback to have more than 200 yards against Michigan this season, but 62 of those yards came on the final drive.

Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht has had no problem dissecting opposing secondaries, throwing for more than 240 yards in four games and 200 yards in five games. The only game he didn't hit that clip was a measly 114 against Wisconsin, and the Badgers are the eighth-best pass defense and second-best in passing yards allowed per attempt.

If Michigan can slow down Becht — the Iowa State transfer who followed head coach Matt Campbell to Happy Valley — and generate turnovers along the way, the Wolverines may be able to rely on their defense for a victory.

articles.title: Sonay Kartal speaks immediately after becoming first British player to reach the Wuhan Open final, ‘I’m very proud’
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal defeated Jelena Ostapenko, 7-6, 7-6, in the Wuhan Open semi-finals. The British star had to work hard for her place in the Wuhan...
articles.body:
Sonay Kartal defeated Jelena Ostapenko, 7-6, 7-6, in the Wuhan Open semi-finals.

The British star had to work hard for her place in the Wuhan Open final, as her Latvian opponent pushed her to the limit. Ostapenko had points to win the first and second sets, but failed to convert them as she grew increasingly frustrated.

Kartal won the match, proving too strong in the two tiebreaks, advancing to the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back after a six-month injury. The 24-year-old was delighted with the result and her performance.

Sonay Kartal reacts after winning 'one of the toughest matches' of her career against Jelena Ostapenko

"Wow, that was probably one of the toughest matches I've played. I knew exactly how she was going to play. At times she's unplayable, and sometimes you just have to ride that wave. Mentally, I think this is one of the best performances I've had in my career, so I'm very proud of that one," said Kartal .

"I was dreaming of playing this match when I was fully fit before the injury, so to be able to come back here in my third event and achieve this is a huge milestone for me. I'm going to recover and enjoy every second of it tomorrow."

Sonay Kartal's record since returning from injury (7-2)

Billie Jean King Cup Finals – Quarter-final (0-1)

The world number 170 was then asked if she had a message for her fans in Wuhan. The crowd was largely in favour of her opponent, Ostapenko, but fans were fair to both players.

"I've said it in every interview: this is an unbelievable court to play on; the atmosphere in every single match has been the most enjoyable experience for me. So, I appreciate everyone who was supporting me today, and hopefully they can come out and do the same tomorrow," said Kartal.

The Chinese fans have warmed to Kartal this week, and fans back home are even more excited. By beating Ostapenko, Kartal became the first British woman to reach the Wuhan Open final.

Kartal is now up to 50th in the 'Live WTA Rankings' and will return to British number one on Monday. She could end the week ranked as high as 36th with a title, which would be a new career-high.

Colin Fleming says Sonay Kartal is the 'coolest woman in Wuhan' as she reaches final

During Sky Sports' post-match coverage, former British tennis star Colin Fleming delivered his verdict on Kartal's big win over Ostapenko in the Wuhan Open semis.

"That's an incredible win; it really is. The coolest woman in Wuhan, and that's what got her through: her ability to just stay in the moment, stay in the present, keep cool, and ultimately outlasting Jelena Ostapenko, who hit 50 winners past her and still couldn't win a set!" he said.

"Sonay Kartal, there's the smile that we saw throughout; that's the biggest one of the day. No wonder, she is into a WTA 1000 final, just a brilliant achievement, and the run doesn't stop here. She's playing the tennis of her life, and she's got every chance of getting her hands on the title."

Kartal will return to play Iga Swiatek or Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's Wuhan Open final. The British star hasn't played either player before on the WTA Tour.

articles.title: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Rams-Cardinals with expert Q&A
articles.summary: Previewing the Rams' upcoming game against Arizona with 5 questions for a Cardinals expert.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have their second divisional matchup of the season this weekend, as they'll host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It's their first meeting with Mike LaFleur's team after he spent the last three years as Sean McVay's offensive coordinator.

To preview this NFC West matchup, we asked Cards Wire lead writer Jess Root five questions, even getting his final score prediction (spoiler: he expects the Rams to win big).

Do the Cardinals have anyone on offense who can beat the Rams besides Trey McBride and Michael Wilson?

Cards Wire: The short answer is no, but other guys will make a few plays. Teagan Quitoriano scored twice last week (his first touchdowns since 2022). Elijah Higgins will be open more as McBride is getting a lot of attention. Kendrick Bourne is reliable. However, none of those guys are players that can be leaned upon for big plays or critical moments.

How big of a blow is Jeremiyah Love's injury?

Cards Wire: Well, he hadn't been given the offense much overall, but the absence of his skillset will make the running game less dynamic. Tyler Allgeier is certainly capable and Bam Knight has had moments for the Cardinals, but Love's absence makes an anemic running game look even less threatening.

Is it still too early for the Cardinals to turn to Carson Beck?

Cards Wire: That is the big debate right now. While Jacoby Brissett hasn't been the problem, he hasn't been good, and after going 2-15 in 17 starts for the Cardinals, he doesn't have much of a ceiling. However, the Cardinals gave him a big raise before the season, so they will keep rolling him out until he isn't best option for them. Many want to see Beck, but with only one start in the preseason, no one knows if he is ready or not.

What are the early reviews of Mike LaFleur as a head coach?

Cards Wire: They are mixed. He sounded good early on, and the offense has had more overall production than last season. However, the defense is terrible. He has become a little less transparent in his answers, and the offense really has been unimpressive with almost no big plays.

Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score?

Cards Wire: Considering the Cardinals' struggles defensively and against the NFC West, it's a blowout with late offense from the Cardinals. Rams 38, Cardinals 24

articles.title: Washington football exploring extra year of eligibility for injured WR
articles.summary: After suffering an injury on Washington's first play of the season, the Huskies are looking to get Christian Moss another year of eligibility.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Christian Moss' 2026 season has been full of bad luck since transferring to the Washington Huskies .

First, the former Kennesaw State standout suffered a hamstring injury that sidelined him for the majority of spring practice. Then, following a strong fall camp, the 6-foot-3 pass catcher suffered a quad injury that forced him to have surgery and, in all likelihood, will end his season.

After the NCAA passed a 5-for-5 eligibility rule over the summer, the injuries could spell an end to his college football career, but Jedd Fisch's coaching staff is exploring a medical exemption to regain his lost year.

"We are working on Christian Moss to see if we can regain a year for him, as it looks as if he will have one play in his final year of college if we're not capable to regain that year for him," Fisch said during his Monday press conference.

If the Huskies are able to regain that year, Moss displayed the skill set of a promising threat from the X receiver spot who can stretch the field and thrives in contested catch scenarios throughout fall camp.

"I think Christian's a dude. He's a dude," Fisch said of Moss during fall camp . "He's made a lot of big-time plays throughout. Got to make them all, but no one makes them all. I'm loving how he's doing. He's taken every rep with the first offense at X, and he's earned that right. He's just somebody that's put himself in position that he's going to be pretty special, I think."

articles.title: Titans vs. Colts: 5 players to start/sit in fantasy football for Week 6
articles.summary: Taking a look at who to start and sit in fantasy football for the Week 6 matchup between the Tennessee Titans and Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will travel to Indianapolis to take on the Colts in an AFC South showdown, giving fantasy football managers several important lineup decisions to consider.

With both offenses looking to find consistency, identifying the players capable of producing despite their respective teams' struggles could make all the difference in Week 6.

The must-start players from this game include Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and tight end Tyler Warren — if he's active.

Josh Downs and Tony Pollard headline this week's recommended starts, while Daniel Jones and Cam Ward are quarterbacks fantasy managers should consider leaving on the bench.

Here's a look at five players to start or sit ahead of Sunday's matchup.

Start 'Em: Josh Downs, WR, Indianapolis Colts

Downs is an intriguing fantasy option heading into Sunday's matchup against a Tennessee defense that has struggled to contain opposing receivers. Downs' ability to create separation underneath and operate effectively out of the slot makes him a valuable target for Daniel Jones, particularly in PPR formats. If Indianapolis can establish a rhythm through the passing game, Downs has the potential to turn a healthy target share into a productive fantasy afternoon.

The biggest factor in Downs' outlook is whether Jones can deliver the football consistently. Although the quarterback's struggles have limited the production of Indianapolis' receiving corps, Tennessee presents an opportunity for the Colts to get their passing attack back on track. Downs is worth consideration as a flex option, especially for managers looking for a receiver with reception upside.

Sit 'Em: Daniel Jones, QB, Indianapolis Colts

Daniel Jones has struggled to provide consistent fantasy production this season, making him a risky option against Tennessee. Through five games, Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions, numbers that leave plenty to be desired for fantasy managers relying on him as their starting quarterback. His inability to consistently generate touchdowns has limited his ceiling, while his recent struggles have also created uncertainty for Indianapolis' passing game.

Although the Titans have allowed opportunities for opposing quarterbacks to produce, fantasy managers should look for more dependable alternatives before trusting Jones in their lineups. His current production makes him difficult to recommend outside of deeper leagues or situations where injuries and bye weeks have severely limited available options. Until Jones demonstrates greater consistency, he's best left on the bench.

Cam Ward has had difficulty finding consistency during his rookie campaign, and Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis presents another challenging test. Ward has recorded 896 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions through five games, and he has yet to throw multiple passing touchdowns in a game this season. Those struggles have prevented him from establishing himself as a reliable fantasy starter, even when the matchup offers some potential upside.

The Colts have shown vulnerabilities against the pass, but Ward hasn't consistently capitalized on favorable opportunities. Tennessee's offensive struggles and difficulty sustaining drives make it tough to trust the rookie's weekly floor. Unless managers are desperate for a quarterback because of injuries or bye weeks, Ward should remain on the bench until he shows signs of improvement.

Start 'Em: Carnell Tate, WR, Tennessee Titans

Carnell Tate remains one of Tennessee's most intriguing fantasy options despite the team's offensive struggles. The rookie leads the Titans with 23 receptions through five games, demonstrating his importance to Ward's passing attack. His nine-catch, 145-yard performance against Baltimore in Week 4 also showcased the upside he can offer when the Titans consistently get him involved in the offense.

Tate's production is tied closely to Ward's ability to deliver accurate passes, which introduces some risk into this recommendation. Indianapolis has been vulnerable against the pass, however, and Tate's established role gives him a path to a useful fantasy performance. Managers should view him as a flex option with upside, particularly in deeper leagues, while recognizing that Tennessee's inconsistent offense could limit his opportunities.

Start 'Em: Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Tony Pollard is worth starting against an Indianapolis defense that has struggled to stop the run. The veteran running back has recorded 273 rushing yards on 68 carries through five games, adding 24 receiving yards on eight catches. Although his overall production hasn't been spectacular, his role as Tennessee's primary running back gives him a reasonable opportunity to accumulate fantasy points through volume.

The Colts have allowed nearly five yards per carry this season, creating an encouraging matchup for Pollard and the Tennessee rushing attack. If the Titans can keep the game competitive and avoid falling into an early deficit, Pollard should have opportunities to contribute throughout the afternoon. His touchdown upside makes him a viable RB2 or flex option, particularly for managers seeking a dependable workload at running back.

articles.title: “I do not want to hear you at all”: Amir Ibragimov reveals fiery Matheus Cunha training incident
articles.summary: Manchester United’s highly rated youngster Amir Ibragimov has discussed his special relationship with Matheus Cunha, revealing details of a tough training-gr...
articles.body:
Manchester United's highly rated youngster Amir Ibragimov has discussed his special relationship with Matheus Cunha, revealing details of a tough training-ground exchange between them.

Regarded as one of the best prospects in Manchester United's youth setup, Ibragimov has been identified as a future star and has frequently trained with the senior squad.

He spoke to club media and shared how tough those sessions can be, particularly describing an incident between him and Cunha.

Ibragimov said, "Bruno [Fernandes] was really helpful, but recently, me and Cunha had a really good connection."

"Like, he helped me a lot because, coming to train with the first team, they are aggressive with you. It's like, because we're young, that doesn't mean they have to let us off, which I think is really good. As soon as I came in, it was straight into tackles, like they don't care how old you are, which, again, I think is really good."

"As soon as I went down, which was a foul but they don't give fouls much [in training] and the coaches just tell you to get on with it. And then Cunha said to me, as soon as I got fouled, 'next time, I do not want to hear you at all. I want you to get up and carry on.'"

Ibragimov continued, "And you know what? Next time I got fouled, I got up straight away and the ball just came to me straight back. And then I scored! He said 'see, this is exactly what I mean.'"

"Then, after that, he was just like talking to me and saying 'as long as you listen and as long as you [learn]'. He said 'if I didn't like you, I wouldn't have helped you.' So I think Cunha, I've had a really good connection with him. He's a really good guy."

United are next in action on Sunday when they face Leeds United at Elland Road.

Beyond the old rivalry, it's a crucial game for Michael Carrick as pressure mounts on him. Manchester United have endured a tough start to the season, amassing just six points from their opening six games.

A defeat would make it difficult for Carrick to recover, given that patience in him and his coaching staff is wearing thin.

articles.title: Davidovich Fokina stuns top seed Zverev to reach Shanghai Masters final
articles.summary: The 26th-ranked Spaniard fought back to win 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 and will play Daniil Medvedev or Rafael Jodar in the final.
articles.body:
Alejandro ‌Davidovich Fokina produced a major upset by defeating top seed Alexander Zverev 5-7 ⁠6-4 6-3 to reach the Shanghai Masters final, where he will face either former world number one Daniil Medvedev or fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar.

The 25th seed fired ⁠36 winners in the two-hour, two-minute contest on Saturday to secure only his second victory over Zverev in eight meetings. His previous win against the German came in the round of ⁠32 at the Canadian Open in 2023.

Davidovich Fokina earned his first break of the match to take the second set, forcing a decider with a stunning backhand passing shot on the run that capped a bruising baseline exchange and brought the crowd to their feet.

Carrying that momentum into ‌the final set, Davidovich Fokina broke Zverev for a 2-0 lead and never relinquished control, booking a place in the second ATP Masters 1000 final of his career after finishing runner-up in Monte Carlo in 2022.

Landing 82 percent of his first serves and repeatedly exposing Zverev on the forehand side, he secured one of the biggest victories of his career.

“I knew that if I stayed there all match, I could get at least ⁠one chance and I took it there in the second set,” ⁠Davidovich Fokina said.

“Then in the third set, I think I was better physically. The early break in the third set gave me a lot of power.

“I focused on just playing, not mattering about the result but enjoying.”

Zverev said fatigue had caught up with him.

“I think a break is quite necessary now,” the 29-year-old told reporters, saying he would monitor his fitness before a tournament in Vienna that begins October 24.

“I carried a little bit of injury, I carried fatigue into the tournament, and I’m OK to lose to a player like this today,” said Zverev, who had felt his ankle at times in Shanghai.

Davidovich ⁠Fokina, who missed the North American hard-court swing in August because of injury, has now won nine consecutive matches in China after ⁠lifting his second tour-level title at the ATP 250 ⁠event in Chengdu last month.

It was a disappointing end to the week for Zverev, a seven-time ATP Masters 1000 champion whose best result in Shanghai remains his runner-up finish to Medvedev in 2019.

The 29-year-old has otherwise enjoyed a ‌fine season, ending his Grand Slam drought at the French Open before claiming a second major title at the US Open and securing the ATP year-end world number one ranking ‌after ‌Jannik Sinner was sidelined for the remainder of the season with a knee injury.

Fifth-seeded Russian Medvedev was playing 12th-seeded Jodar, 20, in the second semifinal.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal: Premier League – preview, teams, prediction
articles.summary: The Gunners failed to score in their last two visits to the City Ground, as both matches ended in goalless draws.
articles.body:
Who: Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal What: English Premier League Where: City Ground, Nottingham, United Kingdom When: Sunday, October 18 , at 4:30pm (15:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 12:30 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Arsenal will try to end their goal drought at the City Ground when they play Nottingham Forest on Sunday – the Gunners failed to score in their last two visits, as both matches ended in goalless draws.

Meanwhile, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said his side had learned lessons from their “extremely average” performance at Brighton before the international break as they returned to winning ways against Leeds last weekend.

The Spaniard was left to stew for 21 days after the 3-0 humbling at the Amex last month – the first defeat of the season for the Premier League champions.

But the Gunners got that performance out of their system at the Emirates last Saturday, coming from behind to beat Leeds 2-1 .

Arsenal also cruised to a 3-0 home win over Lille in midweek to extend their perfect start in the Champions League.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner was beaten on his return to Crystal Palace as Daichi Kamada’s first Premier League goal inspired the Eagles’ 3-1 win last weekend.

Arsenal headed into this weekend in second place in the Premier League, three points behind Manchester City, while Nottingham Forest were 15th.

What happened in Arsenal’s last Premier League game?

Arsenal got back on track as the Premier League champions survived a scare to beat Leeds, although Arteta’s side were in danger of a second successive loss when they fell behind at the Emirates Stadium.

James Justin fired Leeds ahead in the 55th minute after Arsenal failed to clear Gabriel Gudmundsson’s cross.

Arteta had admitted Arsenal were nursing a “pain in the tummy” from the Brighton loss, but Italy defender Riccardo Calafiori found the cure when he converted Ben White’s header from close range in the 62nd minute.

Arsenal showcased their strength in depth as substitute Bruno Guimaraes drilled the winner from the edge of the area just six minutes after coming off the bench.

The Brazilian’s first goal at the Emirates since his close-season move from Newcastle made it five wins from six league matches for the Gunners.

What happened in Forest’s last Premier League game?

Glasner had led Palace to a shock FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City in 2025 and masterminded their UEFA Conference League success in May.

But the 52-year-old Austrian opted to quit Selhurst Park after reported issues with the club’s hierarchy over their transfer policy, opening the way for his move to Forest.

He was greeted warmly by Palace fans before kickoff and it looked like being a victorious return for Glasner when Forest’s Dan Ndoye opened the scoring in the third minute.

But Forest wasted a host of chances to increase their lead and Japan midfielder Kamada levelled in the 41st minute to end his long wait for a top-flight goal.

Jefferson Lerma nodded Palace in front in first-half stoppage time and Yeremy Pino’s 59th-minute goal sent Glasner home empty-handed.

What have the managers said about the game?

“We’re going to try really hard to score goals and to prevent goals as well. It’s going to be a really tough match, they’re an extremely well-coached team.

“We know that, we already have experience with Oliver [Glasner] in the past and they’re a team that at home can create a really special momentum, so we are ready for it.”

“In every game this season [Arsenal] were outrunning the opposition. It’s incredible. The effort and the mindset Mikel [Arteta] has created there is incredible.

“This makes it so tough to play against them and you see it from every single player. They have so many world-class players they can react from the bench.”

The Opta supercomputer has made Arsenal the clear favourites, with a win probability of 58.3 percent. Forest were given a 20.4 percent chance of winning, a draw is 21.3 percent.

The last time Forest beat Arsenal was a 1-0 victory at the City Ground in May 2023, courtesy of a goal by Taiwo Awoniyi, which ended the Gunners’ title hopes that year.

What happened the last time the clubs played?

Arsenal missed a slew of chances in a 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest in January as a dogged defensive performance from Forest and wasteful finishing from the Arsenal forwards meant they took only a point from a game they dominated for long spells.

The best chance of the game fell to Arsenal substitute Bukayo Saka, who headed a Declan Rice cross back towards the far post, but Forest keeper Matz Sels pulled off a superb fingertip save to deny him.

Striker Igor Jesus and defender Nicolo Savona remain unavailable due to calf and knee injuries, respectively.

Key playmaker Morgan Gibbs-White is struggling with a minor muscular problem and is a doubt, while centre-back Nikola Milenkovic is back in training after a knee injury and could feature.

Winger Christos Tzolis (hamstring) and centre-back William Saliba (back) are unavailable for the Gunners.

Arteta said midfielder Martin Zubimendi could be fit to face Forest, but defender Piero Hincapie would likely miss the trip to the City Ground.

The pair suffered freak ankle injuries during a training session on the Emirates Stadium pitch after last week’s win against Leeds.

“Piero is evolving really well,” said Arteta. “Knowing his character and the way he pushes everybody, I’m sure it’s not going to take long, but he will probably need another week or two.

“Zubi looks much better, he already looked much better today. We have another session tomorrow (Saturday) and after that we will assess whether he’s available to play against Forest.”

articles.title: Tiger Woods introduced his children to golf: How Sam and Charlie are shaping the next chapter of his sporting legacy
articles.summary: Explore how Tiger Woods' children, Sam and Charlie, are shaping their own paths in life and sport, with one focusing on academics at Stanford, while the other pursues competitive golf at Florida State University.
articles.body: Tiger Woods’ impact on golf goes far beyond his record-setting accomplishments, major wins and decades of dominance on the PGA Tour. The 15-time major champion has also passed the game down to his children, Sam Alexis Woods and Charlie Axl Woods, providing them with opportunities to play competitive golf while developing interests of their own.But the next chapter of the Woods family sporting legacy is heading in two different directions. Sam has taken the academic route at Stanford University while Charlie has compiled a competitive junior golf resume and signed with Florida State University. Their paths show that Tiger’s influence still determines the family’s relationship with golf without necessitating that the two children take the same routes.Details on Tiger Woods’ children Sam and Charlie and how they forge separate pathsTiger Woods has two children from his ex-wife, Elin Nordegren. They have a daughter, Sam Alexis Woods (born 2007), and a son, Charlie Axl Woods (born 2009). Both children were introduced to the sport at an early age, with one of golf’s most recognizable faces as their father, but their interests went in different directions.Tiger’s busy professional schedule also colored the family’s experience with golf. Sam has previously said she associated the sport with being away from her father due to his tournament commitments. Instead of jumping right into golf as a competitive endeavor, she sampled other sports, such as soccer and track and field.Charlie became interested in athletics at an early age and found himself drawn more and more to golf. He played with his father in professional exhibition events, giving him the chance to learn by direct experience and to be introduced to the competitive environment.Their many options underscore an important distinction: being Tiger Woods’ kids affords an unusual link to golf history, but it does not dictate how either will shape a future. While Sam has made a name for himself through education and personal interests, Charlie is looking for opportunities to compete at the collegiate level.Sam Alexis Woods balances school and family legacySam Alexis Woods has lived a relatively low-key life considering how connected she is to one of the most famous athletes on the planet. Her educational journey has become a major part of her story, with Stanford University being a notable link to her father's university days.Tiger went to Stanford before turning pro in 1996, and was one of the top collegiate players of his generation. She’s at the same university as her dad, so there’s a family connection there, but her focus is academic, so it’s a different sort of experience from the sporting career of her dad, Sam.Golf is not the only sport that has interested Sam. As a child, she played soccer and took up track, broadening her interests outside her father’s professional world. Her story illustrates that a family’s exposure to sport doesn’t necessarily result in a commitment to the same sport.Those moments put her in the public narrative of Tiger’s career without having to become a professional golfer herself. They also demonstrated how family members can assist sporting milestones by supporting and participating rather than competing.Where Sam is now is a compromise between keeping her own goals and staying linked to the legacy of her father. With her Stanford education in her back pocket, she’s heading a different way than Charlie’s competitive golf dreams, but she’s still a part of the sport that influenced much of her childhood via major family events.Since there’s no public info about her longer-term career aspirations, it’s important to distinguish between confirmed educational info and speculation about what she might do after graduating.Charlie Axel Woods takes the competitive golf routeCharlie Axel Woods took a more direct route to competitive golf, honing his game through junior tournaments, high school championships and playing alongside his father. His tournament results have helped cement his place among young golfers, but his surname has also brought attention to his progress.Charlie made his PNC Championship debut with Tiger in 2020 at age 11. The tournament, which pairs major champions with family members, gave the father and son a chance to compete together on a recurring basis. They were the runners-up in 2021, an example of how they could be a contender in a family competition while sharing the course.The next big step came Feb. 10, 2026, when Charlie announced his verbal commitment to play collegiate golf at Florida State University in 2027. The ruling means he will continue his college career at a different school than Stanford, where Tiger played before turning pro and where Sam is studying.The Florida State golf program has produced some great players, including major winner Brooks Koepka. Charlie’s commitment is therefore an opportunity to develop in a competitive college setting while following his individual objectives in the sport. A verbal promise is not the same as actually going through the official process of enrolling in college.Tiger has also talked about how college recruitment has evolved, saying that communication between players, families and coaches has been much faster than during his own recruitment in the 1990s. He has said that being part of Charlie’s decision-making is an opportunity to see the options that his son has gained through his performances.Tiger Woods supports his children's individual ambitionsTiger's role in the sporting lives of his children goes beyond sharing tournament experiences or teaching them golf. He publicly backs Sam’s soccer exploits and Charlie’s golf drills, a nod to a philosophy that allows both kids to chart their own course.Charlie will always be in the spotlight due to his father's achievements, including 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour wins. Yet in collegiate golf, his performances, consistency and development will be judged on their own merits. Sam’s academic journey, too, hints at the Woods family legacy reaching beyond professional rivalry.Tiger's success does not decide the fate of either child. Sam can keep on building her professional and academic identity, and Charlie gets a chance to develop his competitive game at Florida State. Their differing choices show how a sporting legacy can be inspirational, without the next generation needing to follow the same career path.So for Tiger Woods, the next chapter isn’t about whether Charlie will play professional golf someday or whether Sam will become more involved in the sport. It’s also about seeing both kids grow into themselves, while still keeping a connection to the game that has defined so much of his life.Charlie prepares for college golf, while Sam heads to Stanford to continue her education; their paths suggest two different ways of continuing the Woods family story.
