articles.title: Bryce Underwood Has Golden Opportunity to Silence Critics Against Penn State
articles.summary: Bryce Underwood faces a pivotal test against Penn State as Michigan looks to rebound. Can the Wolverines quarterback finally silence his critics? Copy
articles.body:
Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood has heard plenty of criticism during the first five games of the 2026 season. But when Michigan hosts Penn State on Saturday afternoon at the Big House, the sophomore quarterback will have a golden opportunity to remind everyone why he was considered one of the nation's most talented recruits.

The Wolverines enter Saturday's matchup with a disappointing 3-2 record, including an 0-2 start in Big Ten play. Underwood has struggled with consistency, the offense has been difficult to watch, and calls for backup quarterback Tommy Carr have grown increasingly loud.

Now, with Michigan coming off its bye week and Penn State bringing one of the Big Ten's most vulnerable rushing defenses to Ann Arbor, Underwood has an opportunity to change the narrative. The question is whether he can finally deliver the performance Michigan fans have been waiting to see.

Sep 26, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19) passes against the Iowa Hawkeyes during the second half at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Bryce Underwood Has Something to Prove Against Penn State

Through five games, Underwood has completed 59.3% of his passes for 881 yards, five touchdowns, and four interceptions . He has also rushed for 212 yards and two touchdowns, but those numbers have done little to quiet concerns about his development.

The criticism reached another level following Michigan's 20-14 loss to Minnesota on Oct. 3 , when Underwood completed just 10 of 21 passes for 101 yards and two interceptions. Former Michigan tight end Jake Butt was among those who called for Underwood to be benched in favor of Tommy Carr .

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham, however, is sticking with his young quarterback. Despite back-to-back conference losses, Whittingham confirmed that Underwood would remain the starter and that offensive coordinator Jason Beck would continue calling plays.

That decision makes Saturday's matchup especially important. Underwood doesn't necessarily need to throw for 350 yards and four touchdowns, but he does need to show progress in his decision-making, accuracy, and ability to protect the football.

Penn State's Defense Presents a Golden Opportunity

Here's why Saturday could be exactly what Underwood needs.

Penn State enters the matchup allowing approximately 166 rushing yards per game, ranking 105th nationally against the run . Michigan, meanwhile, has struggled to establish its traditional ground attack, averaging just 135 rushing yards per game.

The Nittany Lions' defensive struggles against the run could create opportunities for Underwood, Jordan Marshall, and Savion Hiter. If Michigan can consistently move the football on the ground, it would take pressure off Underwood and potentially create more manageable passing situations.

That could be particularly important against a Penn State secondary that has performed significantly better than its run defense. Michigan would be wise to avoid asking Underwood to win the game with difficult downfield throws when a balanced offensive attack could make his job considerably easier.

Underwood's mobility also gives Michigan another weapon to exploit Penn State's defensive weaknesses. Designed quarterback runs, read-option concepts, and play-action opportunities could help the Wolverines establish an offensive rhythm that has been missing for much of the season.

Michigan Needs Bryce Underwood to Deliver

The pressure surrounding Underwood isn't going away anytime soon, particularly with Carr waiting for an opportunity. Earlier this month, we highlighted the growing debate surrounding Michigan's quarterback situation as frustration continued to mount following the loss to Minnesota.

But Michigan's offensive problems extend well beyond one player. The Wolverines have struggled to run the football consistently, protect their quarterback, and avoid costly mistakes, which means Underwood hasn't exactly been operating in ideal circumstances.

Saturday presents an opportunity for everyone involved to start turning things around. A productive rushing attack, improved offensive line play, and smarter decisions from Underwood could go a long way toward restoring confidence in an offense that has underperformed expectations.

What Underwood Needs to Show Against Penn State

And make no mistake, Underwood doesn't have to be spectacular to accomplish that goal. He simply needs to demonstrate that he can manage the offense, make timely throws, avoid unnecessary turnovers, and help Michigan win football games.

Penn State enters Saturday with a 3-3 record and an 0-3 mark in Big Ten play, meaning both programs desperately need a victory. For Underwood, however, the stakes feel even more personal because another disappointing performance would almost certainly intensify the calls for a quarterback change.

The talent that made Underwood such a highly regarded recruit hasn't disappeared. Now he has to prove that he can translate that ability into consistent production when Michigan needs it most.

Saturday's matchup against Penn State might be Underwood's best opportunity yet to silence his critics. Whether he takes advantage of it could have a significant impact on the direction of Michigan's season.

articles.title: Chelsea goalie Dibu Martinez taken to hospital after head injury vs. Everton
articles.summary: Chelsea goalkeeper Dibu Martinez was conscious leaving the field but was taken to the hospital for additional evaluation, his manager said.
articles.body:
A head injury Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano "Dibu" Martinez suffered in the Blues' 2-0 win over Everton on Saturday, Oct. 17 was serious enough for the Argentina international to be taken to the hospital, with the club waiting to see his status.

Martinez was racing off his line to a claim a set piece in the 66th minute, when Everton center back Jarrad Branthwaite tried to put a header on the ball but instead made contact with the goalkeeper.

That led to a long delay as Martinez was given medical attention for nearly 10 minutes, with Mike Penders replacing him in the 75th minute after Martinez left the field on a stretcher.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said Martinez was alert as he left the field but that additional studies were underway to understand what injury he'd suffered and what the next course of action needs to be.

"As far as I know, he left the stadium conscious. Right now he's in the hospital doing some precautionary tests," the Chelsea coach said. "So, let's see, but this is what I know so far."

Chelsea won the game thanks to a double from Pedro Neto, who scored just after the second half started and just before the match ended to help the club secure its fourth win of seven matches so far this year.

While the injury clearly was something that caused Chelsea to take every precaution, some Everton fans remained unconvinced the oft-provocative goalkeeper wasn't simply wasting time, with boos heard on the broadcast as the stretcher started to take Martinez off the field.

articles.title: Ex-NBA coach draws John Stockton, Deron Williams connection to Jazz rookie Darryn Peterson
articles.summary: As the Utah Jazz prepare for the 2026-27 NBA season, former head coach Tyrone Corbin believes rookie Darryn Peterson could follow in the footsteps of franch...
articles.body:
As the Utah Jazz prepare for the 2026-27 NBA season, former head coach Tyrone Corbin believes rookie Darryn Peterson could follow in the footsteps of franchise legends John Stockton and Deron Williams.

Following Utah's 3-1 preseason finish, which included a 119-116 victory over the Phoenix Suns on Friday night, Corbin highlighted the organization's history of building around talented guards while discussing Peterson's potential.

In a recent interview with Kyle Odegard of NEXTPredict, Corbin drew connections between the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and two of Utah's most accomplished point guards.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"They had another guard there for a lot of years, John Stockton , and did a lot of great things with him. And another guard in Deron Williams , who did a lot of great things there. They have a history of taking point guards and building around him. Hopefully that continues with him."

Meanwhile, Williams established himself as one of the league's premier point guards during his six seasons with the Jazz, earning two All-Star selections before his departure in 2011.

Tyrone Corbin sees John Stockton, Deron Williams blueprint for Jazz rookie Darryn Peterson

Although Peterson has considerable ground to cover before approaching either player's accomplishments, his preseason performances offered an early glimpse of his potential.

The 19-year-old averaged 13.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 3.8 turnovers across four appearances while playing 25.5 minutes per game. He shot 44.4% from the field, 21.4% from 3-point range and 76.9% from the free-throw line.

Peterson delivered his strongest performance during Utah's 117-106 loss to the Denver Nuggets, recording 23 points, three rebounds and three assists while shooting 10-for-18 from the field in 30 minutes.

Beyond Peterson's individual potential, Corbin expressed confidence in Utah's approach to developing its young roster rather than rushing its rebuilding process.

"It's Utah. They don't overreact or go really fast. They'll pace themselves and hopefully they hit on a couple of these young kids, build from the inside and have a chance to be better sooner than later."

With Peterson joining a young core featuring Ace Bailey and Keyonte George, the Jazz have several promising pieces to build around as they look toward their long-term future.

Utah will open its 2026-27 regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against the Memphis Grizzlies on the road at 5 p.m. PT.

articles.title: Why was Yehor Yarmolyuk sent off and why didn’t Liverpool get a penalty?
articles.summary: The ball was not in play while Yehor Yarmolyuk moved his head towards the face of Jeremy Jacquet before a corner
articles.body:
Brentford midfielder Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for "violent conduct" towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet in the box.

But Liverpool did not receive a penalty because it took place while the players were waiting for a corner to be delivered and the ball was not in play.

The incident occured in first-half stoppage time and as Brentford led Liverpool 1-0 thanks to Lewis Keane-Potter's earlier header.

But the hosts were reduced to 10 men after Jacquet went down in the box holding his face and referee John Brooks was sent to the pitch-side monitor by the VAR.

After watching replays of the incident, Brooks decided that Yarmolyuk had committed a butting action when he bumped into Jacquet and moved his head towards the Frenchman.

A similar incident took place last week at Old Trafford when Rodrigo Bentancur moved his head towards Luke Shaw's face and the Tottenham midfielder was also sent off.

Brooks announced on the pitch that Yarmolyuk had been sent off for a "headbutt action" but that it would remain a Liverpool corner.

The incident was the second VAR intervention of the match after Brooks awarded Liverpool a penalty, only to overturn his decision at the pitch-side monitor.

Meanwhile, Dominik Szoboszlai 's return from injury lasted just 32 minutes as the influential midfielder was forced off after for what appeared to be a recurrence of the issue.

articles.title: When will Aaron Philo return for Florida?
articles.summary: Philo got hurt during last week's loss to South Carolina
articles.body:
Florida will likely be without its starting quarterback for its clash against Texas. Aaron Philo, who suffered a shoulder injury during last week's loss to South Carolina, will sit today with Tramell Jones Jr. getting his first start, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel .

While Philo won't start, it's possible he could be available off the bench. Thamel reports Florida will determine if Philo can play in pregame warmups.

Jones, a sophomore and former three-star recruit, didn't exactly light it up after entering the game for an injured Philo last week. The backup completed six of his eight passes for only 40 yards, tossing an interception as well.

Here's what we know about Florida's quarterback situation as the Gators hope to end their two-game skid.

Jones is a 6-foot, 196-pound quarterback out of Jacksonville, Florida. He's appeared in seven games across two seasons, completing 44 of his 64 passes for 443 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions.

Since Philo could possibly play off the bench today, it wouldn't be shocking to see him return next week vs. Georgia.

articles.title: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury
articles.summary: The Bruins are without their top signal-caller for the season.
articles.body:
The 12th-ranked UCLA football team is off to an impressive start under head coach Bob Chesney. But the Bruins will have to continue without starting quarterback Nico lamaleava. The former five-star quarterback is out for the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury in UCLA's victory over Oregon last week.

The injury is a significant setback for the undefeated Bruins, who entered the week with a 5-0 record. With unprecedented postseason hopes on the line, UCLA must now adjust its offense as it prepares to face Wisconsin on Saturday.

Iamaleava injured his left knee late in the second quarter against Oregon. He was tackled by Bear Alexander and Jerry Mixon while scrambling, with his leg appearing to twist during the play. UCLA's medical staff attended to the quarterback, who returned for one more play and threw an interception. However, he did not return to the field after halftime and was later seen without his uniform.

Although UCLA had not officially confirmed his status earlier this week, Chesney acknowledged there was "serious concern" about the quarterback's condition.

Iamaleava's absence leaves a significant gap in UCLA's offense. His ability to extend plays has helped the Bruins escape difficult situations, while his mobility forces opposing defenses to account for the passing game. This also creates opportunities for the rushing attack. He finishes the season with 982 passing yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions on 72-of-116 passing. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.

UCLA has two possible replacements for Iamaleava. Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach and Nico's younger brother, Madden lamaleava. Dieffenbach replaced the injured starter against Oregon, completing three of six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown.

Chesney indicated that Dieffenbach would get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin.

articles.body:
PSG have rotated their team heavily to take on Strasbourg in Ligue 1 this afternoon, with a largely second string on the pitch.

If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

It's become almost impossible to guess Luis Enrique's starting XIs for Ligue 1 games.

The coach loves to rotate in these domestic games, and he's constantly keeping people guessing with his moves through the whole team.

The fact that he has such good options in every position means he can vary the lineup massively without losing any strength.

Maghnes Akliouche scores his first PSG goal. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

For today's game against Strasbourg, it was known in advance that Marquinhos wasn't going to play. But his changes have actually gone much further than that. It's as close to a second string as you'll see from the coach.

Of course Tuesday night's game against Barcelona is a huge factor in his thinking.

Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, Fabian Ruiz, Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, Willian Pacho and Achraf Hakimi jointheir captain Marquinhos in missing out.

That means the team has Matvey Safonov in goal, with a back four featuring Lucas Digne and Warren Zaire Emery at full back, with Ilya Zabarnyi and Lucas Hernandez at centre back.

In midfield, Dro Fernandez makes his latest appearance, alongside Joao Neves. It looks like Lucas Beraldo will sit behind them.

The front three has Ferran Torres leading the line, flanked by Khvicha Kvaratshelia and Maghnes Akliouche.

That is a team that is still packed with world class quality, despite the rotation.

Marquinhos is not in the team to face Strasbourg this afternoon as Luis Enrique continues his strict rotation policy.

Maghnes Akliouche probably won't get the start today – but that doesn't mean his manager isn't delighted with his progress.

articles.title: Who will be the Bears starting quarterback vs. Falcons? What Ben Johnson said
articles.summary: Caleb Williams is back practicing with the Chicago Bears as he recovers from a hamstring injury. Here's what he and Ben Johnson said about his status.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson continues to keep the playing status of top quarterback Caleb Williams a mystery.

Johnson was asked Friday, Oct. 16, if his star, who has been out since Week 2 with a hamstring injury, will play in a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons

Williams returned to practice this week, including Friday, shortly after Johnson spoke with reporters.

"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Johnson said. "He looked good yesterday for one practice, but, we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back."

Madden cover athletes by year, from Eddie George to Caleb Williams

Johnson, who has been mysterious about his starting back throughout most of Williams' absence, said the focus is on making sure no effects of the injury linger.

"Confidence is a big part of it as well, but I know he wants to play," Johnson said. "He's a competitor. It's been not fun for him the last few weeks watching from the sideline, just like any guy that loves football. It's been a tough deal for him. I know he's itching to get back out there and help us win ball games. If we feel really good as a front office, a coaching staff, and the player himself about playing, then we'll go ahead and go with it."

Williams sparked optimism among fans by reposting a video on TikTok on Friday that referenced his comeback, but he did not provide any additional information on a timeline.

"Before you start asking, I do not know if I'm playing yet," Williams said Thursday. "I have to go through a bunch of medical protocols; obviously have to get out there and practice, do the stress testing that you do when you're trying to come back from injury or serious injury. That's first."

Who will start for the Bears if Caleb Williams can't play?

The Bears have a 2-1 record in the three games since Williams' injury with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum at quarterback.

Johnson was equally cryptic about who might start if Williams can't play against the Falcons.

"We've got two guys that are equally qualified," he said.

Keenum, 38, led the Bears to a 27-7 Week 3 victory over the Eagles after Bagent was ruled out with a concussion. He completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and three total touchdowns (two passing, one rushing).

Bagent then led Chicago to a 23-12 victory over the Jets in Week 4, completing 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards, though he did throw an interception. He struggled against the Packers the following week, completing just 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards before being benched for Keenum in a 31-7 drubbing.

Below is a full look at Chicago's quarterback depth chart, which currently runs four-deep.

Jacob Camenker contributed to this report.

articles.title: Füllkrug's second-half brace rescues draw for Bremen against Paderborn
articles.summary: Werder Bremen had to battle back and save parity against a clinical SC Paderborn this afternoon at the Weserstadion. Two first-half goals from the visitors m...
articles.body:
Werder Bremen had to battle back and save parity against a clinical SC Paderborn this afternoon at the Weserstadion. Two first-half goals from the visitors made for a chorus of whistles at the interval, but Niclas Füllkrug's brace ensured a share of the spoils.

Making home advantage count in the initial exchanges, it seemed near inevitable that Bremen would open the scoring as Niclas Füllkrug flashed wide. Minutes later, only Nahuel Noll stood between Marco Grüll and Chucki from reasonably gilt-edged positions.

In a blink of an eye, however, Paderborn established a 2-0 lead. Grüll's mix up on the ball allowed Steffen Tigges to feed Stefano Marino. The 22-year-old driving into the right side of the box with speed before arrowing the ball into Karl Hein's top-right corner.

Things got even better for Ralf Rangnick's men when Tigges himself netted on the half-hour. Bremen's rearguard were caught napping, letting a long throw bounce into the box for a routine toe-poke finish. Another Noll parry crucially kept out Arthur before the interval.

Making one change at the breeak, Daniel Thioune's side halved the deficit just before the hour. A diagonal ball flicked on by Eren Dincki sat up nicely for Niclas Füllkrug to snap the ball inside the lower-left post. Suddenly the half-time boos made way for support.

Mitchell Weiser's bench impact proved telling 7 minute later. His cross yielded a penalty after Laurin Curda's handball. Füllkrug stuck it away to take his season tally up to six. Paderborn also emptied the bench, bringing on Pieringer, Baack, Phillipe and Müller

Bremen pushed to complete the comeback with Weiser and Arthur testing Noll from tight angles. Paderborn also had their chances to snatch it late on. Four minutes of injury time left Rayan Philippe with a shot that struck the post and bounced ensuring it stayed a draw.

articles.title: Five bold predictions for Ravens-Browns with Tyler Huntley starting
articles.summary: Here are five bold predictions as the Ravens face the Browns in a pivotal AFC North matchup.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens head into Sunday's AFC North matchup with the Cleveland Browns knowing that divisional games rarely follow a comfortable script. Still, the atmosphere is positive. Baltimore comes off an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons .

The circumstances surrounding this team remain complicated. Injuries continue to test its depth, and Tyler Huntley is preparing to lead the offense again after Lamar Jackson was ruled out for another week .

The Browns present their own challenges, particularly with Todd Monken now leading them and Deshaun Watson showing signs of renewed confidence. Still, Baltimore has reasons to believe it can control this matchup.

The Ravens have found ways to win on the road. Their running game remains a strength. If Baltimore takes care of the football and controls the line of scrimmage, it could create separation late. Here are five bold predictions for the Ravens' Week 6 trip to Cleveland.

Tyler Huntley throws two more touchdown passes

The Cleveland Browns have allowed every opposing quarterback they've faced to throw at least one touchdown pass, and there's little reason to assume that trend will suddenly end against Baltimore. Huntley threw two touchdown passes in the Ravens' overtime win over the Falcons, giving the offense a timely boost while Jackson remains sidelined. The Ravens converted eight of 15 third downs and converted three red zone trips into touchdowns

Another two-touchdown performance would be a meaningful step for Huntley as he gets another week of practice with the starters. Familiarity with the offense and improved timing could help him play with greater confidence, particularly if Baltimore establishes the run and creates favorable passing situations. Cleveland's defense won't make it easy, but Huntley has a chance to build on last week's performance. The conditions are set for another solid afternoon.

Baltimore wins the time-of-possession battle comfortably

Cleveland has struggled to control the clock this season, winning the time-of-possession battle just once. Even in that game, the Browns held the ball for only 30:07, and they haven't exceeded 30 minutes of possession in any other contest.

Baltimore has the personnel to exploit that weakness. The Ravens entered Week 6 averaging 164.4 rushing yards per game through their first five contests, giving them a reliable foundation to sustain drives and keep Cleveland's offense on the sideline. If Derrick Henry and the rushing attack establish themselves early, Baltimore can dictate the game's pace, stack points, and make it harder for the Browns to mount a comeback.

Watching the New York Jets sack Watson eight times in Week 5 should give Baltimore's defense plenty of encouragement. The Ravens don't necessarily need to match that total to make a difference, but four sacks would be a substantial contribution against a Cleveland offense that has struggled to keep its quarterback clean.

Watson has been sacked 19 times so far this season. Baltimore must balance pass-rush aggression with discipline against Watson's mobility, especially after defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver emphasized the importance of maintaining assignments and finishing plays.

If the Ravens can generate pressure without giving Watson easy escape routes, they could force hurried decisions and create opportunities for the secondary. Trenton Simpson also has a chance to contribute and add another sack to his already impressive 2026 resume.

Baltimore enters this matchup with a plus-three turnover margin, while Cleveland sits at minus-one. That difference gives the Ravens another reason to believe they can create separation, especially if they protect the ball and force the Browns into late-game chances.

The prediction is that Cleveland plays relatively clean football early, keeping the game competitive while trying to take advantage of its home field. If Baltimore builds a second-half lead, however, the Browns may feel compelled to push the ball downfield and make riskier decisions. That could lead to a late giveaway or two, allowing the Ravens to turn a close game into a more comfortable finish.

This matchup could remain tight through the first half, as divisional games often do, but Baltimore has the running game and defensive playmakers to pull away after the break. If Huntley protects the football, Henry controls the clock, and the defense creates consistent pressure, the Ravens can gradually wear down Cleveland and capitalize on mistakes.

An overtime finish isn't necessary this time. Baltimore's last two-score win came in Week 1, and the Ravens have a chance to deliver another decisive result by closing out a strong road game. The Browns may make it a grind, but the Ravens' ability to control the ground game and generate pressure should prove decisive. Baltimore improves to 5-1 with its win. Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 17.

articles.title: Muheim produces late magic again as Hamburg stun Stuttgart
articles.summary: Despite facing their third away fixture in just seven days, Sebastian Hoeneß’s Stuttgart side started brightly in Hamburg, dominated possession early, and cr...
articles.body:
Despite facing their third away fixture in just seven days, Sebastian Hoeneß's Stuttgart side started brightly in Hamburg, dominated possession early, and created several promising chances.

But, it was Hamburg who posed the initial attacking threat, as Fabio Vieira intercepted a misplaced pass from Angelo Stiller in the fifth minute but failed to convert, sending his shot wide of Dennis Seimen's goal.

The visitors gradually asserted themselves, with Deniz Undav meeting a delivery from Bilal El Khannouss and directing it over the crossbar with his shoulder; shortly after, Hamburg-born Ermedin Demirovic headed another cross from the Moroccan wide in the 15th minute.

Stuttgart dominated possession in the opening stages, holding over 80%, but Merlin Polzin's side grew into the contest and nearly took the lead in the 27th minute when a corner from Miro Muheim found Sebastian Bornauw, whose header deflected off Vieira and Seimen made an impressive save.

The visitors kept the pressure on and came closest to breaking the deadlock six minutes before the interval, as a well-executed counterattack let Jamie Leweling pick out Undav in the penalty area, but the Stuttgart captain's first-time effort hit the post.

Demirovic then saw a header denied by Daniel Heuer Fernandes, ensuring that both teams entered the interval goalless.

Yousuff Poulsen nearly scored for the hosts three minutes into the second half, striking the post following a lofted pass from David Moller Wolfe.

As in previous fixtures in Paderborn and Bratislava, Stuttgart sought to regain control early in the second half, though Hamburg had begun to gain the upper hand.

Six minutes after his earlier attempt, Poulsen came closest to scoring, his shot striking the bar after a touch from VfB goalkeeper Seimen, while less than a minute earlier, Demirovic had sent a header just inches wide.

As has been the theme of the season, the match became an end-to-end contest after Stuttgart's early dominance, with HSV looking increasingly threatening.

They had an effort in the 58th minute when Undav attempted an acrobatic volley that Heuer Fernandes denied, as the half continued at a frenetic pace and the Volksparkstadion anticipated the opening goal.

Heading into the weekend, a point would have been perfect for HSV, but they could well have sensed a missed opportunity in the second half had they not found the net.

In the 88th minute, they finally punished Stuttgart, with Muheim hammering in from range and catching Seimen off guard with a ripper, his second late strike in a week after netting against Hoffenheim last time out.

For Stuttgart, it is hard to argue that anything other than defeat was deserved. Once again, they surrendered control in the second half and struggled to get a grip as the pace increased.

Hoeneß will carry those concerns into the Atletico Madrid clash midweek, while Hamburg can celebrate their first clean sheet of the season and their second home win of the term, fully recovering from a dismal start.

articles.title: 3 Things to Watch in Chargers-Chiefs: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston are good to go in Week 6
articles.summary: Can Chris O’Leary and the Chargers defense continue their strong play against another elite defense?
articles.body:
It's Chargers-Chiefs this week and as much as I'd like to be able to say this one is for sole possession of first place in the AFC West, I cannot. One team is winless and the other is undefeated.

This one does not look good on paper. By records alone, it also doesn't look like a fun watch for anyone that isn't already a fan of either team.

But hey, it's a divisional matchup that has given us plenty of entertaining watches over the last decade. More than likely this one will still do the same.

That said, here are three things I'll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday.

1.) What will the offense look like just one week before the bye?

There's a very strong chance the Chargers simply play it safe with their numerous injuries and use this week as one more opportunity to see what the bottom of the roster has within them.

Wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Brenen Thompson are all hobbled and have been limited through the first two practices this week. Tre' Harris is in even worse shape as he has been a DNP thus far.

KeAndre Lambert-Smith just had his 21-day window activated and it looks like he's trending to return this week. That development may lead the Chargers to take a cautious approach with their top guys just one week from the bye.

Let's just be honest, the offense honestly looks no better no matter who is out there unless it's a healthy McConkey. He hasn't been healthy since Week One and it's about time we let him get to 100 percent before he steps back out on the field.

Right now, Justin Herbert's healthy receivers are Theo Wease, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling. On the practice squad, they have Gary Jennings and the recently-signed Luke Grimm. Jennings is out of game day elevations which means he'd have to be signed to the active roster in order to participate against the Chiefs. With Alec Ingold now on IR, Jennings could take that spot if the team chooses.

As for the offensive line, will they send out four rookies for another week? Will veteran Daniel Brunskill learn the offense enough to start at right tackle for Alex Harkey? We'll have to see come game day.

UPDATE: Both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were removed from the final injury report meaning Justin Herbert will have his two top wideouts back this Sunday.

2.) Will Omarion Hampton continue to see his snaps share decrease?

Hampton played only 31.7 percent of the offense's snaps against the Broncos, although he did receive over 40 percent of the running back carries.

With each week, Hampton is playing less and less. Kimani Vidal's huge 42-yard touchdown rumble will not do him any favors in getting back anywhere lose to workhorse duties. It also doesn't help that Mike McDaniel continues to force Keaton Mitchell into the game plan to run sweeps to specifically the right side.

Defenses know what's coming when either back is in, which can't be good for a Chargers offense that already isn't fooling anyone in anyway.

The Chiefs have a great defense. Their linebackers can fly, hit hard, and blitz. Chris Jones is still a menace along the interior and George Karlaftis is an ascending pass rusher. They're about to face a very young Chargers offensive line and it may not even matter which running back is in.

Hampton, in my opinion, is still the Chargers' most talented back. I don't think he's a timeshare guy and his ability to punish deep into the fourth quarter was an aid to the Bolts last season as they closed out games with the ball in their hands. It'd be nice to get back to that kind of football. But seeing how things are going, we may never see that again (at least, maybe until next year?).

3.) Can Chris O'Leary's defense continue their strong start against another elite offense?

After a rough outing in Week One against the Cardinals, O'Leary's unit has been one of the best in the entire league the past four weeks.

Despite not having Derwin James and Donte Jackson in their past two games, they're still a top-1o unit in EPA/play, success rate, and dropback/EPA.

The efficiency is insane for a group that's far and away the leader in most drives started within their own territory (18!). Compared to the Saints who are second with 11, that's even more unreal.

They got Josh Allen and the Bills to turn the ball over five times and helped put a lid on both Sam Darnold and Bo Nix the past two weeks. Now they will face Patrick Mahomes and the revitalized Chiefs offense that now features Kenneth Walker and a highly-productive rushing attack.

O'Leary doesn't need the team to win this game for it to be a personal "W" in his book. If the defense does their part, records a turnover or two, and helps keep this one close, no one will be able to say another word about his group not pulling their weight.

articles.title: Neto’s brace fires Chelsea past Everton but Martinez head injury mars win
articles.summary: Argentinian international taken to hospital for precautionary tests after head clash with Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite.
articles.body:
Pedro Neto’s double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emi Martinez to a head injury.

Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half on Saturday and secured the three points during the 11 added minutes following the lengthy treatment given to the stricken Martinez.

The Argentinian international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital.

“As far as I know he left the stadium conscious. Right now he’s in the hospital doing the precautionary tests, so let’s see,” said Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso .

A first away win of the season lifts Chelsea above the Toffees into the top four and the Blues also recorded a first clean sheet in 23 Premier League games.

“We needed one of these wins away. We have played very professional, very serious, looking solid. It is a very good win,” added Alonso.

“We need to get many more clean sheets for the rest of the league games but for sure the first one of the season feels good and now we need to keep going this way.”

After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards.

That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game.

Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish’s cross too close to Martinez.

Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner.

Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England teammate James Garner.

That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period.

Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Jordan Pickford.

Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet since January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options, despite the loss of Martinez.

“I just felt that Chelsea had that little bit more flair and ability which we didn’t possess at the right moments today,” said Everton boss David Moyes.

The treatment for Martinez threatened to halt Chelsea’s momentum as they controlled the second half.

Belgian Mike Penders replaced the Chelsea number one for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses.

At the other end Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro.

But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson’s free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall.

“We are really ‌‌pleased. Shame for Emi but we wish you all the best. This win is for him,” Neto told TNT Sports after his first Premier League brace.

“We need a clean sheet, to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike did as well.”

articles.title: ESPN insider hammers home belief that Vikings could make a trade
articles.summary: Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings continues to get linked to his former team in trade rumors.
articles.body:
Jauan Jennings has yet to make an impact in his first season with the Minnesota Vikings . He has played in four of the team's five games, amassing only two catches for nine yards.

He was visibly frustrated on the sideline of last Sunday's win over the New Orleans Saints , with cameras catching him pounding the Superdome turf. Speculation since then has fueled potential trade rumors as the Vikings approach their Week 6 bye.

On Wednesday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler became the latest reporter to speculate that Jennings could be traded to the San Francisco 49ers, where he played his first six seasons.

"Jauan Jennings is the forgotten man in Minnesota's passing attack," Fowler wrote. "He would fit well with any Shanahan-style scheme, which is much of the league now."

The 49ers would make sense for Jennings, as he is familiar with them. But it'd be hard to imagine the Vikings being willing to part with Jennings this early in the season and send him to the only other undefeated team in the NFC.

Jennings still has time to settle into his role in the offense. Let's hope Kevin O'Connell can utilize him coming out of the bye week with an offense that should be much healthier than it was early in the season.

articles.title: Chicago Bears @ Atlanta Falcons: Week 6 Players to Watch
articles.summary: Take a look at @BryanOrenchuk’s players to watch for Atlanta as the Bears visit the Falcons in week 6.
articles.body:
Last week I discussed which Packer players to watch and I greatly hope there aren't as many Falcons jumping off the screen like there were Cheeseheads in Lambeau.

Remember, in this weekly series, I'm featuring one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think will be critical to their team's success. Like seasons past, you won't see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team's success. I'll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time.

Gotta start with a familiar face on the Falcons defense.

The former 2nd round selection by Ryan Poles in the 2023 NFL Draft out of the University of Florida appears to be on his way to his best season as a pro after showing substantial improvement in run game and continuing to make his presence felt in the passing game. And to say he will be slightly motivated to prove that moving on from him was a bad move would be the most obvious statement of the season. If Gervon can disrupt Caleb's return by generating interior pressure in both the run and passing games, Atlanta could hold Chicago within reach to keep this one close. But if Garrett Bradbery and his two stud sidekicks Joe Thuney and Johah Jackson can keep Dexter a non-factor like he was far too often in his Bears tenure, then Bears GM Ryan Poles might get to add another feather in his cap – especially if Grady Jarrett continues his high level of play against his former team on Sunday as well. Check out this nice breakdown by Chicago Bears Central on X.

Everyone knows this team runs through All-World running back, Bijan Robinson. And that Drake London and Kyle Pitts are the only other blue-chip players on the roster. But does everyone know that Jahan Dotson is quietly putting together his most impressive season and carving out quite the roll for himself in this Falcons offense? Jahan, just 26 years of age this season, is leading the Falcons in yards per reception at 18.6 yards per catch and has had two consecutive games at 27 yards per reception. Considering how badly the Packers gashed the Chicago secondary deep, Dotson will need to be contained in this one. How will Dennis Allen do this will be fascinating to watch, but hopefully Kyler Gordon is healthy enough to take his men deep as he will likely get a good bit of snaps lined up opposite Dotson this week if so. If Dotson can continue taking the top off the defense and provide the timely spark for this Falcons offense, Caleb and co might have to put up 40 points to win this one. Otherwise, Chicago should be able to comfortably outduel the Falcons with a hobbled Michael Penix under center.

What about you? Did Poles make a mistake getting rid of Dexter? Who will you be focused on this week in the ATL?

articles.title: 10 Atlanta Falcons Prospects to Watch For Week 7 of College Football
articles.summary: Here are the 10 prospects we’re keeping an eye on for the Falcons in today’s college football matchups.
articles.body:
Welcome to the meat and potatoes of the college football season. This Saturday, the cream of the crop will show up in multiple ranked matchups, along with a few ranked-vs.-unranked games featuring real talent that may pop up in the 2027 NFL Draft.

With most of the cupcakes out of the way, several draft picks have big games ahead in Week 7 of college football, but here are 10 prospects Atlanta Falcons fans should watch.

Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, IN – 12 pm EST – Fox

While Charlie Becker may be the more well-rounded prospect, Nick Marsh has the tools a quarterback like Michael Penix might find appealing. He wins on out-breaking routes; he snaps his head and hips at the top of the route, forcing separation and making himself an immediate target for quarterbacks who throw with anticipation, like Penix. Overall, Marsh projects as a solid X or Z receiver in a Tommy Rees offense, allowing Drake London to move around the formations and unlock even more production.

DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium – Austin, TX – 12 pm EST – ABC

6'6", 300 pounds is not supposed to move as it does for Florida defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. A former English basketball player, Oyebadejo is still a raw prospect who needs to learn some of the nuances of the defensive line. However, Oyebadejo already has the raw movement skills, power, and quickness needed to be a high-end prospect.

Tiger Stadium – Baton Rouge, LA – 12 pm EST – ESPN

Having a big body at safety is always an advantage; when that safety can play the run like a linebacker, it adds another layer of versatility to the defense. Isaac Smith is a big safety at 6'0", 220 pounds, and he can come in on day one and add to the special teams unit with his ability to find a ball carrier and bring him to the turf.

Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee vs. Alabama

Neyland Stadium – Knoxville, TN – 3:30 pm EST – ABC

The Falcons have done a sensational job getting the most out of their defensive line, largely thanks to the synergy between defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich and defensive line coach Nate Ollie. Gervon Dexter and Brandon Dorlus are two of the best at the position right now at getting pressure on the quarterback, but adding a rookie like Xavier Gilliam to the rotation would be a dream come true. At 6'2", 305 pounds, Gilliam is having the best season of anyone at the position; he has 11 tackles for loss, 22 QB pressures, and 16 run stops, according to PFF. Gilliam's blend of speed and strength is extremely tantalizing.

Patrick Kutas, OL, Ole Miss vs. Missouri

Vaught-Hemingway Stadium – Oxford, MS – 3:30 pm EST – SEC Network

The offensive line will need more depth as Stefanski's offensive vision becomes clearer. Patrick Kutas has played every position on the line except for left tackle, dating back to his time at Arkansas. As a right guard at Ole Miss, he's started to find his niche on the interior, relying more on his technique to succeed. His hands don't have much pop, but they're enough to turn defenders where he needs them.

Audavion Collins, CB, Penn State @ Michigan

Michigan Stadium – Ann Arbor, MI – 3:30 pm EST – CBS

I've been looking for bigger cornerbacks for the Falcons to bring in because they seem to struggle against big, physical receivers, mostly because of the size of both Terrells and Mike Hughes. I'm throwing all of that away because of how Penn State's Audavion Collins has played heading into this week. Listed at 5'11", 185 pounds, he has allowed only two catches on seven targets through six games and has showcased elite speed and footwork that keep him in position to make a play on the ball.

LaVell Edwards Stadium – Provo, UT – 7:30 pm EST – ABC

Coming into this season, one of the hotter names at cornerback was Evan Johnson, especially after his Pop-Tart Bowl performance, where he allowed only one catch on six targets and recorded an interception. At 6'0", 181 pounds, Johnson has had a fine start to the 2026 season, but he gets the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and superstar quarterback C.J. Carr in primetime. This could be a breakout game in a big moment for BYU.

Patrick Overmyer, TE, Houston vs. Oklahoma State

TDECU Stadium – Houston, TX – 7:30 pm EST – Fox

If the Falcons want to add more of a receiving option to the tight end room, Houston's Patrick Overmyer would be a great addition. Last week against Kansas State, he had nine receptions for 83 yards and four touchdowns, all in the red zone. Atlanta could use another consistent red zone threat like Overmyer, especially if he can show more as a run blocker before the year ends.

Memorial Stadium – Norman, OK – 7:30 pm EST – SEC Network

I understand that Ryan Neuzil is putting some of his best work on tape, but he still is going to be a free agent next season, and who knows if Ian Cunningham and company will pay the premium that may be necessary to keep him in house. If they want to look in a different direction, Kentucky's Coleton Price may be an avenue to explore, especially if he has a good day against Oklahoma's David Stone.

Autzen Stadium – Eugene, OR – 11 pm EST – Fox

It takes a lot of discipline to play cornerback in a zone-heavy scheme, it takes a lot of patience and football IQ, and there aren't many that play off a receiver better than Nebraska's Andrew Marshall. Even when in traditional man, he's ot the technique to stay attached to the hip of his receiver, leading him to one of the better allowed passer ratings in the country.

Which prospects are you keeping an eye on Saturday? Which of these players would be the best fits for Atlanta? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Today’s Irish Fan Game Plan: Contain BYU’s Bear Bachmeier
articles.summary: This week, One Foot Down asked our connected Notre Dame football fans to weigh in on what they say is the biggest obstacle to the Irish prevailing in Provo t...
articles.body:
This week, One Foot Down asked our connected Notre Dame football fans to weigh in on what they say is the biggest obstacle to the Irish prevailing in Provo today.

We heard from 53 respondents, and almost six out of every ten said: Box in Bear Bachmeier, beat BYU.

Bachmeier is 77-for-106 for 1,o33 yards, with eight passing touchdowns against one interception. The sophomore can create chaos with his legs as well, rushing for 239 yards on 36 attempts and four additional touchdowns. The Irish haven't yielded a rushing touchdown yet this year. Could the streak break today at Bachmeier's behest?

About one-quarter of respondents said they thought the altitude would be the Irish's Provo problem. LaVell Edwards Stadium sits 4,649 feet above sea level, which is the eighth highest in college football. For comparison, the Irish play their home games at Notre Dame Stadium, which sits about 723 feet above sea level. Will the Irish be left gasping for breath as BYU runs tempo? And will this be most apparent in the first quarter, the fourth, or never at all?

Just four percent of respondents picked the Cougars running backs, but I do have to wonder if that percentage would have been far greater if BYU's best, L.J. Martin, were playing today. Martin, the Big 12's Offensive Player of the Year in 2025, leads the team in rushing with 344 yards on 44 attempts. He also caught five balls for 41 yards as a receiver. The Cougars will rely today on redshirt junior Preston Rex and freshmen Journee Tonga and DeVaughn Eka.

On this week's podcast , Joshua, Brendan and myself all picked Notre Dame to cover the 10.5 point spread. Now is your time to weigh in. You can head over to FanDuel , the sponsor of this post, and lock in your pick and you can leave it in the comments below.

articles.title: Jaguars 'have not indicated' they will trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.
articles.summary: A report from The Athletic shared the latest intel on the Jacksonville Jaguars and WR Brian Thomas Jr.
articles.body:
"All eyes" are on Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. with the NFL trade deadline on the horizon.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic put together his weekly 'what he's hearing' article, and included was a section on Thomas Jr.'s standing with the Jaguars .

Trade speculation around Thomas Jr. has again ramped up in recent weeks, and following the recent Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, eyes are now on the Jaguars' wide receiver.

However, Jacksonville remains firm in saying that they won't trade Thomas Jr.

"The Jaguars have not indicated they will part with their 2024 first-round pick, even after he caught zero passes for zero yards in last week's win against the Eagles ," Jones wrote. "His name continues to come up in conversations around the league as Parker Washington solidifies himself as the Jags' top wideout. Jacksonville hasn't been in a rush to deal Thomas, and I suspect that will remain the case until we get closer to the trade deadline."

Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are the top two options at receiver for the Jaguars, while the addition of Nate Boerkircher at tight end has led to more heavy personnel groupings. The emergence of rookie Josh Cameron has earned him more snaps as well.

The end result of all that for Thomas Jr. is that there have been fewer opportunities. Through five games, Thomas Jr. has caught just nine passes for 105 yards with a touchdown. He has only three receptions over the last three games.

While Thomas Jr. thrived as a bona fide No. 1 target as a rookie, this Liam Coen system isn't predicated on having that presence; rather, the scheme operates most efficiently when the ball is being spread around.

That said, there's no reason for the Jaguars to trade Thomas Jr. just for the sake of doing so. Even if the ball doesn't go his direction, his presence is still valuable, with the attention that he draws as a downfield target helping to open up opportunities elsewhere on offense.

articles.title: Jake Fraser-McGurk blazes to 14-ball fifty in One-Day Cup, misses Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's world record
articles.summary: Jake Fraser-McGurk made history by scoring the fastest half-century in One-Day Cup history. His incredible innings of 122 runs off just 63 balls, supported b...
articles.body:
Australian batter Jake Fraser-McGurk produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing the fastest half-century in One-Day Cup history as South Australia posted a commanding 397/7 against Queensland at the Karen Rolton Oval in Adelaide on Saturday. The 24-year-old opener raced to his fifty in just 14 deliveries, breaking his own tournament record. He eventually scored 122 off 63 balls, hammering 10 fours and nine sixes to put South Australia in a dominant position. His effort also ranks among the joint fourth-fastest half-centuries in List A cricket, with India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi holding the world record for the fastest fifty, off just 11 balls. Fraser-McGurk found an equally impressive partner in South Australia captain Nathan McSweeney, who registered his third List A century with a composed 106 off 103 balls. Their efforts helped the hosts finish with a formidable total in their 50 overs.

Fraser-McGurk wasted little time taking control of the innings. He plundered 22 runs from Tom Straker's second over before launching an assault on Tom Whitney in the fourth, striking two sixes and a four. The Australian brought up his half-century in the sixth over with a boundary off Hayden Kerr and continued his onslaught, racing to 75 off just 22 deliveries. With the fastest List A century in sight, he briefly threatened to surpass his own record of reaching three figures in 29 balls. However, after surviving a couple of chances, Fraser-McGurk tempered his aggression before accelerating again. He smashed two consecutive sixes off Whitney and brought up his century in just 49 deliveries. His explosive knock finally ended at 122 in the 21st over when Kerr dismissed him, but the opener had already provided South Australia with a flying start.

While Fraser-McGurk supplied the fireworks, McSweeney anchored the innings with a well-paced century. The South Australia skipper struck 106 off 103 balls, reaching his third List A hundred and ensuring the hosts maintained their momentum after the opener's dismissal. Fraser-McGurk's performance also continued his remarkable record at the Karen Rolton Oval. Across six List A innings at the Adelaide venue, he has accumulated runs at an average of 68.66 and a strike rate of 204.97, including two centuries and a half-century. His record-breaking innings, combined with McSweeney's contribution, gave South Australia a strong platform as they finished on 397/7 against Queensland.
